definition_zh: 错误；差错；误差
definition_en: a mistake, or the state of being wrong
core_image: 一支箭偏出靶心，落在旁边的空处
scene: 表格里有一个小错误，导致总数不对。A small error in the table made the total wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 error 是「错误」（第 1 个义项：做错或写错的地方）；句意：表格里有一个小错误，导致总数不对。

derivatives.zh: 错误的
犯错；出错
无差错的

senses.title: A mistake
senses.definition: something done or written wrongly
senses.definitionCN: 做错或写错的事情
senses.example: She spotted an error in the first line.
senses.exampleCN: 她发现第一行有一个错误。
senses.why: The Latin noun means a wandering, so an error is a step that has strayed from the right way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词意为「游荡」，所以错误就是偏离正路的一步。

senses.title: The state of being wrong
senses.definition: the condition of holding a wrong belief or being mistaken
senses.definitionCN: 持有错误看法或弄错的状态
senses.example: I was in error about the meeting time.
senses.exampleCN: 我把会议时间弄错了。
senses.why: The word can name not only the mistake but the condition of being mistaken.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不仅指错误本身，也可以指弄错的状态。

senses.title: A measured deviation
senses.definition: a difference between a measured or calculated value and the true value
senses.definitionCN: 测量或计算值与真实值之间的差异
senses.example: The experiment allows a small margin of error.
senses.exampleCN: 这项实验允许有一个小的误差范围。
senses.why: Scientific use turns the general mistake into a measurable deviation.
senses.whyCN: 科学用法把一般性的错误转化为可测量的偏差。

intro.en: Error comes from Latin error, a wandering or mistake, from errare, to wander.
intro.cn: error 来自拉丁语 error（游荡、错误），源于 errare（漫游）。

items.en: Errare means to wander or go astray.
items.cn: errare 意为游荡、走偏。

items.en: Error means a wandering or a mistake.
items.cn: error 意为游荡或错误。

items.en: Errur carries the word into French.
items.cn: errur 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Error names a mistake in English.
items.cn: 中古英语 error 指错误。

items.en: Modern English adds scientific and computing errors.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了科学误差与计算机错误。

note.en: Error is the noun of straying, close to err, erroneous, and to ordinary mistake words.
note.cn: error 是表示「走偏」的名词，与 err、erroneous 以及普通的「错误」词相邻。

entries.definition: to make a mistake
wrong
wandering or straying

normalIntro.en: Error is a wandering step: the mind or hand leaves the straight road for a moment.
normalIntro.cn: error 是走偏的一步：头脑或手在一瞬间离开了直路。

normal.en: To make an error is to get something wrong.
normal.cn: make an error 就是把某事弄错。

normal.en: Human error causes many accidents.
normal.cn: 人为失误造成许多事故。

normal.en: An error message tells you the program failed.
normal.cn: error message 告诉你程序出错了。

normal.en: In error means by mistake.
normal.cn: in error 表示错误地。

normal.en: Compare mistake: mistake is everyday, error is slightly more formal and technical.
normal.cn: 对比 mistake：mistake 更日常，error 稍正式且更技术化。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow landing just beside the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭落在靶心旁边。

abstract.en: Imagine a pen slipping on a single letter.
abstract.cn: 想象笔尖在一个字母上滑了一下。

abstract.en: Think of a clock running a few seconds fast.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟快了几秒钟。

examples.en: The report contains several spelling errors.
examples.cn: 报告里有几处拼写错误。

examples.en: He sent the parcel to the wrong address in error.
examples.cn: 他误把包裹寄到了错误的地址。

examples.en: Scientists try to reduce the margin of error.
examples.cn: 科学家努力缩小误差范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「err + or」——走「偏」了，就是犯错；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 errare（游荡、走偏）→ error（游荡；错误）→ 古法语 errur → 英语 error，核心义「偏离正途」。

sensesIntro.en: Error first means a wrong act or word, then the state of being mistaken, and finally a measurable deviation.
sensesIntro.cn: error 先指做错的事或写错的地方，再指弄错的状态，最后指可测量的误差。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow that lands beside the target.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭落在靶心旁边。

branches.en: A concrete mistake is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 具体的错误是日常义项。

branches.en: Being mistaken is the state sense.
branches.cn: 弄错的状态是状态义项。

branches.en: A measured deviation is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 测量偏差是技术义项。

branches.en: A person in error often makes a visible mistake.
branches.cn: 处于错误中的人往往会犯下可见的错误。

branches.en: Both a slip and a margin of error are deviations from the true value.
branches.cn: 小失误与误差范围都是对真实值的偏离。

intro.en: Error is a Latin wandering noun, with English err, erroneous, and errorless built around it.
intro.cn: error 是拉丁语中表示「走偏」的名词，英语围绕它构成 err、erroneous 与 errorless。

latinIntro.en: Latin errare means to wander, and error means a wandering or mistake.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 errare 意为游荡，error 意为游荡或错误。

items.example: Errare gives the straying image.
Error is the direct source.
Err is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: err 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: Error keeps the noun sense.
The suffix -eous forms erroneous.
Erroneous describes wrong content.
The suffix -less forms errorless.
Errorless means free of mistakes.
Errant shares the wandering root.

definition_zh: （火山）喷发；喷出（熔岩、气体、灰）；突然爆发（怒气、笑声、暴力）；突然出现（皮疹）；（牙齿）萌出
definition_en: to burst out suddenly, especially of a volcano throwing out lava and ash, or of anger, laughter, noise, a rash or a tooth breaking through
core_image: 地下的压力积到极限，黑色山口忽然撕开，火光、灰柱与石块一起冲向天空
scene: 火山观测站的屏幕上，地表微微鼓起，仪器指针剧烈跳动。 The volcano began to erupt just after midnight, throwing ash high above the island.
sceneCN: 这里 erupt 指火山喷发（第 1 个义项：熔岩、气体与火山灰从火山口猛烈喷出）；句意为那座火山在午夜刚过时开始喷发，把火山灰抛到岛屿上空。

pos.zh: （火山）喷发；喷出（熔岩、气体、火山灰）
突然爆发（怒气、笑声、掌声、暴力）
突然出现（皮疹、斑点）；（牙齿）萌出

derivatives.zh: 喷发；爆发；皮疹
喷发性的；突发的；发疹的
破裂；断裂（同出拉丁 rumpere，强调撕裂）
打断；中断（inter- 加 rumpere，本义「在中间断开」）
腐蚀；使腐败（cor- 加 rumpere，本义「彻底破坏」）
突然的；生硬的（ab- 加 rumpere，本义「被折断」）

senses.title: A volcano bursts open
senses.definition: to send out lava, ash and gas suddenly and violently from a volcano
senses.definitionCN: 火山突然而猛烈地喷出熔岩、火山灰与气体
senses.example: Mount Etna erupted again last night, closing the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 埃特纳火山昨夜再次喷发，导致机场关闭。
senses.why: erupt comes from Latin erumpere, to break out, from e- out plus rumpere to burst; a volcano literally breaks through its own sealed throat.
senses.whyCN: erupt 来自拉丁 erumpere「冲出」，由 e-「出」加 rumpere「破裂」构成；火山正是冲破自己封闭的通道。

senses.title: Anger or laughter bursts out
senses.definition: to express a strong feeling suddenly and with force, especially anger or laughter
senses.definitionCN: 猛然有力地表达强烈情绪，尤指愤怒或大笑
senses.example: The crowd erupted in laughter at the mimic's first line.
senses.exampleCN: 模仿者一开口，人群就爆发出笑声。
senses.why: the same break-out image moves from rock to feeling: something held under pressure finally leaves the body.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「冲破」意象从岩石移到情绪：被压住的东西终于冲出体外。

senses.title: A rash appears suddenly
senses.definition: to appear suddenly on the skin as a rash or spots
senses.definitionCN: 以皮疹或斑点的形式突然出现在皮肤表面
senses.example: A red rash erupted across his arms after the hike.
senses.exampleCN: 徒步之后，他双臂突然起了一片红疹。
senses.why: medicine borrowed the volcano image: the skin surface is where hidden irritation breaks out.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了火山的意象：皮肤表面正是隐藏的刺激「冲破」出来的地方。

senses.title: A tooth breaks through the gum
senses.definition: of a tooth, to push through the gum and become visible
senses.definitionCN: 指牙齿顶破牙龈、露出表面
senses.example: Her first molar erupted without any trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一颗臼齿顺利萌出，没有不适。
senses.why: a tooth literally breaks out of the gum, so the Latin sense of bursting through fits exactly.
senses.whyCN: 牙齿确实从牙龈里「破出」，拉丁语「冲破而出」的本义完全吻合。

senses.title: Violence or conflict breaks out
senses.definition: to start suddenly and violently, of fighting, protest or conflict
senses.definitionCN: 指打斗、抗议或冲突突然而猛烈地开始
senses.example: Protests erupted in several cities after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 声明发布后，数个城市突然爆发抗议。
senses.why: a conflict that erupts appears without warning, like a vent opening in ground thought to be quiet.
senses.whyCN: 爆发的冲突毫无预兆地出现，就像看似平静的地面忽然裂开一个喷口。

senses.title: A geyser shoots up
senses.definition: of a geyser or hot spring, to send a column of water and steam into the air
senses.definitionCN: 指间歇泉或温泉把水柱与蒸汽喷向空中
senses.example: The geyser erupts every ninety minutes or so.
senses.exampleCN: 这处间歇泉大约每九十分钟喷发一次。
senses.why: hot water under pressure behaves like magma: it waits, then breaks out through a narrow channel.
senses.whyCN: 受压的热水和岩浆一样：先积蓄，再从狭窄通道冲破而出。

senses.title: A sound or applause breaks out
senses.definition: of a sound, cheer or applause, to begin suddenly and loudly
senses.definitionCN: 指声音、欢呼或掌声突然而响亮地开始
senses.example: Applause erupted the moment the curtain fell.
senses.exampleCN: 幕布落下的瞬间，掌声骤然响起。
senses.why: sound also has a moment of breaking through silence, and the verb marks that sudden start.
senses.whyCN: 声音也有「冲破寂静」的一刻，这个动词标记的正是那突然的起点。

senses.title: Liquid or gas spurts out
senses.definition: of liquid, gas or steam, to come out forcefully through a narrow opening
senses.definitionCN: 指液体、气体或蒸汽从狭窄开口有力地喷出
senses.example: Steam erupted from a crack in the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸汽从管道的裂缝中喷出。
senses.why: the physical core remains: a substance under pressure finds a small opening and leaves it fast.
senses.whyCN: 物理核心仍在：受压的物质找到一个小开口，迅速冲出去。

intro.en: Erupt comes from Latin eruptus, the past participle of erumpere, to break out, built from e- (out) and rumpere (to break). English borrowed it in the seventeenth century; the volcano sense came first, and the emotional, medical and acoustic senses followed.
intro.cn: erupt 来自拉丁 eruptus，即 erumpere「冲出、破出」的过去分词，由 e-「出」与 rumpere「破」构成。英语于十七世纪借入，最早用于火山喷发，情绪义、医学义与听觉义随后扩展。

items.en: Rumpere meant to break, burst or tear apart. Its past participle ruptum gives the stem rupt- seen in rupture, interrupt, corrupt, abrupt and bankrupt.
items.cn: rumpere 意为「打破、爆裂、撕裂」。其过去分词 ruptum 提供 rupture（破裂）、interrupt（打断）、corrupt（腐蚀）、abrupt（突然的）、bankrupt（破产的）中所见的 rupt- 词干。

items.en: The prefix e-, shortened from ex-, meant out of or forth; joined to rumpere it produced erumpere, to break out.
items.cn: 前缀 e- 是 ex- 的缩略，意为「向外、出来」；与 rumpere 结合构成 erumpere「破出」。

items.en: Erumpere was used for soldiers bursting from a gate, for water breaking from a pipe, and for a buried force escaping its container.
items.cn: erumpere 曾用于士兵冲出城门、水冲破管道，以及被压住的力量脱离容器而出。

items.en: The participle eruptus described what had burst out; the noun eruptio named the bursting forth and gives English eruption.
items.cn: 分词 eruptus 描述已经冲出的东西；名词 eruptio 指「冲出」这一事件，衍生英语 eruption（喷发）。

items.en: English took the verb in the seventeenth century. Early examples describe volcanoes and wounds; the sense of a sudden outbreak of feeling is later.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个动词。早期例子描述火山与创口；情绪突然爆发的义项出现较晚。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the Latin forms themselves are recorded and the root is not in doubt, but the exact first date of each English sense is only approximate, with the emotional sense arriving later. Rupture keeps the plain sense of tearing, so it is a cousin in root rather than a synonym.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：拉丁形式本身有记录，词根无争议；但各英语义项的确切首见年代只能给约数，其中情绪爆发义出现较晚。rupture 保留「撕裂」本义，因此只是同根近亲，并非同义词。

note.en: Group one shares the Latin stem rupt-; group two holds verbs of sudden outward release.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词干 rupt-；第二组是表示突然向外释放的动词。

entries.definition: From ab- (away) plus rumpere: literally broken off, hence sudden or brusque, with no preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ab-「离开」加 rumpere 构成：本义「被折断」，因此表示突然、生硬、毫无铺垫。

entries.definition: A tearing or bursting of something under strain, such as a pipe, a tendon or a treaty; it stresses the tear itself.
entries.definitionCN: 受力之物撕裂或爆开，如管道、肌腱或条约；强调撕裂本身。

entries.definition: From inter- (between) plus rumpere: to break into something between its parts, hence to cut a conversation short.
entries.definitionCN: 由 inter-「之间」加 rumpere：在部分之间插入断开，因此指打断谈话。

entries.definition: From com- (thoroughly) plus rumpere: morally broken through, hence dishonest or decayed.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「彻底」加 rumpere：道德上被彻底折断，因此指腐败、败坏的。

entries.definition: From Italian banca rotta, a broken bench: a merchant's table smashed, hence unable to pay debts.
entries.definitionCN: 来自意大利语 banca rotta「折断的凳子」：商人的摊桌被砸，因此指无力偿债、破产的。

entries.definition: To blow up with a report, from a chemical or nuclear reaction; erupt stresses emergence through an opening rather than a bang.
entries.definitionCN: 因化学反应或核反应而伴巨响炸开；erupt 强调从开口冲出，而非一声爆响。

entries.definition: The general English verb for breaking open from inside; erupt is its geological and dramatic counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 表示由内向外破开的日常动词；erupt 是其地质与戏剧化的对应词。

entries.definition: To send out large amounts of something, often violently and messily; it fits the lava and gas sense closely.
entries.definitionCN: 大量、常常猛烈而杂乱地喷出某物；与熔岩与气体的义项很贴合。

entries.definition: To release pressure or feeling through an outlet; the focus is on the opening and the relief, not the burst.
entries.definitionCN: 通过一个出口释放压力或情绪；重点在出口与缓解，而非爆开。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: e- means out and rupt- means broken: erupt is the broken-out event.
normal.cn: e- 是「出」，rupt- 是「破」：erupt 就是「破出」这一事件。

normal.en: The rupt- family is large: eruption, eruptive, rupture, interrupt, corrupt, abrupt, bankrupt.
normal.cn: rupt- 家族很大：eruption（喷发）、eruptive（喷发性的）、rupture（破裂）、interrupt（打断）、corrupt（腐蚀）、abrupt（突然的）、bankrupt（破产的）。

normal.en: Volcano phrases fix the first sense: a volcano erupts, lava erupts, ash erupts from the vent.
normal.cn: 火山搭配固定第一义：火山喷发、熔岩喷出、火山灰从喷口喷出。

normal.en: Body phrases fix the medical sense: a rash erupts, a tooth erupts, spots erupt on the skin.
normal.cn: 身体搭配固定医学义：皮疹发出、牙齿萌出、皮肤上冒出斑点。

normal.en: Emotion phrases take a phrase of manner: erupt in laughter, erupt with anger, erupt into violence.
normal.cn: 情绪搭配后面常接表示方式的短语：爆发出笑声、勃然大怒、突然演变为暴力。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed kettle whose lid lifts without warning.
abstract.cn: 想象一只密封的水壶，盖子毫无预兆地被顶开。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet classroom where one laugh sets off the whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的教室里，一声笑把整间屋子点燃。

abstract.en: Picture a pinhole in a hot pipe and a white jet cutting the air.
abstract.cn: 想象热管道上的一个针孔，白色气流割开空气。

examples.en: The volcano erupted for the first time in a century, forcing nearby villages to evacuate.
examples.cn: 这座火山一世纪以来首次喷发，附近村庄被迫撤离。

examples.en: She erupted in anger when the results were announced.
examples.cn: 结果公布时，她勃然大怒。

examples.en: A rash erupted on his back after he touched the plant.
examples.cn: 他碰过那株植物后，背上突然起了一片疹子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）加 rupt（破）」——地底的压力破壳而出 → 喷发、爆发、突然冒出

root: 拉丁 rumpere「破裂」加前缀 e-「出」构成 erumpere「冲破而出」，其过去分词 eruptus 直接进入英语作 erupt；名词为同源的 eruptio（喷发）。同族含 rupture（破裂）、interrupt（打断）、corrupt（腐蚀）、abrupt（突然的）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all record the same instant: something sealed gives way and its contents leave fast. The first and sixth are geological, the second, fifth and seventh put the burst in feeling, streets and sound, the third and fourth place it on the body, and the eighth keeps the plain physical jet.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项记录的都是同一个瞬间：封闭之物让开，里面的东西迅速冲出。第一与第六义属地质，第二、第五与第七义把爆发放在情绪、街巷与声音里，第三与第四义落在身体上，第八义保留最朴素的物理喷射。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed chamber under pressure whose wall finally gives way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个受压的封闭腔体，壁面终于让开。

branches.en: GEOLOGICAL VENT: a volcano and a geyser both wait under pressure, then open a channel.
branches.cn: 地质喷口：火山与间歇泉都先受压等待，再打开通道。

branches.en: FEELING AND CONFLICT: anger, laughter and street fighting all leave the body or the crowd at once.
branches.cn: 情绪与冲突：怒气、笑声与街头打斗都一下子离开身体或人群。

branches.en: BODY SURFACE: a rash and a tooth both become visible by breaking through a covering.
branches.cn: 身体表面：皮疹与牙齿都靠冲破一层覆盖物才被看见。

branches.en: SOUND: applause breaks the silence exactly as lava breaks the crust.
branches.cn: 声音：掌声打破寂静，正如熔岩冲破地壳。

branches.en: MATTER UNDER PRESSURE: gas and liquid find a narrow crack and leave it at speed.
branches.cn: 受压物质：气体与液体找到狭窄裂缝，高速离去。

intro.en: Erupt is a Latin compound verb: a prefix of direction plus a verb of breaking, with the participle supplying the English form.
intro.cn: erupt 是一个拉丁复合动词：方向前缀加「破」动词，英语形式取自其过去分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin rumpere, erumpere, eruptus and eruptio supply erupt, eruption and the wider rupt- family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rumpere、erumpere、eruptus 与 eruptio 衍生 erupt、eruption（喷发）以及整个 rupt- 词族。

items.structure: e- (Latin prefix, shortened from ex-, 'out, forth')
items.example: The prefix e- marks movement out of a container.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 e- 标记「离开容器向外」的运动。

items.example: Every word in the rupt- family carries a break.
items.exampleCN: rupt- 词族的每个词都带着一个「破」义。

items.meaning: to break out; to burst forth
items.example: The vent began to erupt at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 喷口在黎明时开始喷发。

senses.title: A volcanic eruption
senses.definition: a sudden release of lava, ash and gas from a volcano into the air or onto the surface
senses.definitionCN: 火山把岩浆、火山灰与气体突然释放到空中或地表
senses.example: The eruption sent a column of ash high above the island.
senses.exampleCN: 这次喷发把一根灰柱送到岛屿上空的高处。
senses.why: eruption comes from Latin eruptio, a bursting forth, from erumpere, to break out, so a volcano literally breaks out of its crust.
senses.whyCN: eruption 来自拉丁 eruptio「冲出」，出自动词 erumpere「破出」，因此火山字面上就是冲破地壳而出。

senses.title: An outbreak of rash on the skin
senses.definition: the sudden appearance and spread of a rash over the body as part of a disease
senses.definitionCN: 作为疾病的一部分，皮疹在全身突然出现并蔓延
senses.example: Measles brings a widespread eruption that starts behind the ears.
senses.exampleCN: 麻疹会引起一片广泛的皮疹，先从耳后开始。
senses.why: the old medical use is native to the word: Latin eruptio already named skin lesions breaking out, long before it named mountains.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法是这个词固有的：拉丁 eruptio 早在指火山之前，就已经指皮肤病变的暴出。

senses.title: A tooth breaking through the gum
senses.definition: the process by which a developing tooth pushes through the gum and appears in the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 发育中的牙齿顶穿牙龈、出现在口腔中的过程
senses.example: The dentist charted the eruption of the first molars.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医记录了第一磨牙的萌出情况。
senses.why: a tooth physically breaks through tissue, so the same image of breaking out applies without any change of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 牙齿确实顶破组织而出，因此同一个「破出」意象直接适用，词义无需变化。

senses.title: A violent outburst of feeling
senses.definition: a sudden, forceful expression of anger, laughter or other strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 愤怒、笑声或其他强烈情绪的突然有力表露
senses.example: His eruption of anger silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他怒火的爆发让全场安静下来。
senses.why: what was held under pressure breaks out, exactly as magma does, so the metaphor needs no new vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 被压住的东西破壳而出，与岩浆完全一样，因此这个比喻不需要新词。

senses.title: A geyser's jet
senses.definition: a periodic burst of hot water and steam from a geyser or hot spring
senses.definitionCN: 间歇泉或温泉周期性喷出的热水与蒸汽
senses.example: The geyser's eruption lasts about four minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这眼间歇泉的喷发持续约四分钟。
senses.why: pressurised water finds a narrow opening and shoots out, which is the same physical story as a volcano without the magma.
senses.whyCN: 受压的水找到狭窄开口后冲出去，这与火山是同一个物理故事，只是没有岩浆。

senses.title: A sudden flood of something abstract
senses.titleCN: 抽象事物突然大量涌现
senses.definition: a sudden large appearance of praise, data, complaints or similar things
senses.definitionCN: 赞誉、数据、抱怨之类事物突然大量出现
senses.example: The film brought an eruption of praise from critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片引来影评人一片赞誉。
senses.why: the count noun was extended to anything that arrives suddenly and in quantity, keeping the image of something bursting out.
senses.whyCN: 这个可数名词被扩展到一切突然且大量到来的事物，保留了「冲出」的意象。

senses.title: A single spot on the skin
senses.definition: one small lesion or pimple on the skin, as counted and described by a clinician
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上的一处小病变或小脓疱，由医生计数并描述
senses.example: A single eruption appeared on the forearm and faded in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 前臂上出现了一处皮疹，一周内消退。
senses.why: medicine counts what breaks out, so the mass event and the individual spot share one noun.
senses.whyCN: 医学要对冒出的东西计数，因此整体暴发与单个斑点共用同一个名词。

senses.title: Gas or liquid escaping under pressure
senses.definition: a sudden escape of steam, gas or liquid through a weak point or opening
senses.definitionCN: 蒸汽、气体或液体通过薄弱处或开口突然逸出
senses.example: A sudden eruption of steam cracked the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸汽的骤然喷出使管道开裂。
senses.why: the core event is material breaking out of a container, and a pipe is only a smaller container than a mountain.
senses.whyCN: 核心事件是物质破开容器而出，而管道只是一个比山更小的容器。

intro.en: Eruption comes from Latin eruptio, a bursting forth, from erumpere, built from e-, out, and rumpere, to break. The same rumpere supplies rupture, interrupt, corrupt, abrupt and, through French and Italian, bankrupt.
intro.cn: eruption 来自拉丁 eruptio「冲出」，出自动词 erumpere，由 e-「出」与 rumpere「破」构成。同一个 rumpere 还衍生出 rupture、interrupt、corrupt、abrupt，并经法语与意大利语衍生出 bankrupt。

items.en: Rumpere meant to break or burst; its past participle ruptus supplied the stem rupt- that runs through the whole family.
items.cn: rumpere 意为打破或爆裂；其过去分词 ruptus 提供了贯穿整个词族的词干 rupt-。

items.en: The prefix e-, out, plus rumpere made erumpere, to break out or burst forth, used for anything escaping a container.
items.cn: 前缀 e-「出」加 rumpere 构成 erumpere，意为破出、冲出，用于任何从容器中逸出之物。

items.en: Eruptio named the act of bursting out; medical Latin used it for rashes breaking out on the skin before geology used it for mountains.
items.cn: eruptio 指「冲出」这一动作；医学拉丁语用它指皮肤上暴出的皮疹，比地质学用它指火山更早。

items.en: English borrowed eruption in the seventeenth century, at first chiefly in medical writing about rashes and fevers.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 eruption，最初主要用于论皮疹与热病的医学写作。

items.en: The volcanic sense became dominant later, and the word then spread to geysers, teeth, emotions, crowds of praise and escaping steam.
items.cn: 火山义后来成为主导，这个词随后扩展到间歇泉、牙齿、情绪、如潮的赞誉与逸出的蒸汽。

items.en: Source uncertain (first use only): the earliest English examples are chiefly medical and the date of the volcanic sense is given only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首用义）：最早的英语例证主要是医学用法，火山义的年代只能给约数。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin breaking stem; group two holds near neighbours for sudden outbursts and their results.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「破」词干的词；第二组是表示突然爆发及其结果的近义词。

entries.definition: To burst out suddenly; eruption is the noun of that action, so the pair differs only in word class.
entries.definitionCN: 突然冲出；eruption 是这一动作的名词形式，两者只差词类。

entries.definition: Tending to burst out, or produced by an eruption; it describes a quality or origin rather than the event.
entries.definitionCN: 易爆发的，或由喷发造成的；描述性质或来源，而非事件本身。

entries.definition: A tear or burst of a pipe, tendon or membrane; it shares the breaking stem but lacks the outward prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 管道、肌腱或膜的撕裂或破裂；共用「破」词干，但没有表示向外的前缀。

entries.definition: To break into something in progress; the prefix inter- puts the break between two things rather than outward.
entries.definitionCN: 打断正在进行之事；前缀 inter- 让断裂发生在两者之间，而非向外。

entries.definition: A sudden release of strong feeling or activity; it is commoner than eruption for laughter or rage and rare for volcanoes.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈情绪或活动的突然释放；用于笑声或愤怒时比 eruption 更常见，用于火山则少见。

entries.definition: A violent expansion driven by a chemical or nuclear reaction; it implies blast energy, not merely material escaping.
entries.definitionCN: 由化学或核反应驱动的猛烈膨胀；强调爆炸能量，而不只是物质逸出。

entries.definition: A strong sudden wave of air or heat from an explosion; it names the pressure effect rather than the outpouring.
entries.definitionCN: 爆炸产生的突然强气流或热浪；指压力效应，而非喷出物。

entries.definition: The sudden start of disease, war or violence; it overlaps with eruption in medicine but not in geology.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病、战争或暴力的突然开始；在医学上与 eruption 重叠，在地质上则不重叠。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: e- out plus rupt- break: to break out, and the noun names that breaking out.
normal.cn: e-「出」加 rupt-「破」：破壳而出，名词就指这个破出的动作。

normal.en: The rupt- family runs eruption, erupt, eruptive, rupture, interrupt, corrupt, abrupt and bankrupt.
normal.cn: rupt- 词族包括 eruption、erupt、eruptive、rupture、interrupt、corrupt、abrupt、bankrupt。

normal.en: Volcano phrases: a volcanic eruption, an explosive eruption, the eruption column.
normal.cn: 火山搭配：火山喷发、爆炸式喷发、喷发柱。

normal.en: Medical use survives: a skin eruption, a drug eruption, the eruption of a tooth.
normal.cn: 医学用法仍在：皮疹、药疹、牙齿萌出。

normal.en: Word class pair: lava erupts, so the result is an eruption; the verb is erupt, not erupt.
normal.cn: 词类配对：岩浆喷出，结果就是一次喷发；动词是 erupt，名词才是 eruption。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed jar of fermenting liquid with a crack in the lid.
abstract.cn: 想象一只密封的发酵罐，盖子上有一道裂缝。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom where one joke sets off a wave of laughter.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室，一个笑话引发一阵笑声。

abstract.en: Picture an inbox that goes from two messages to hundreds overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个收件箱，一夜之间从两封变成数百封。

examples.en: The eruption forced the airline to cancel every flight to the island.
examples.cn: 这次喷发迫使航空公司取消了所有飞往该岛的航班。

examples.en: A drug eruption covered her arms within hours of the first dose.
examples.cn: 首剂用药后数小时内，药疹就布满了她的双臂。

examples.en: The announcement produced an eruption of questions from the audience.
examples.cn: 这项宣布引来听众一片问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋rupt（破）」——压力从里面破壳而出 → 喷发、爆发

root: 拉丁 eruptio ← erumpere（e-「出」+ rumpere「破」）→ eruption；同族含 erupt、rupture、interrupt、corrupt、abrupt、bankrupt。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one gesture: something held inside breaks out. The event is volcanic, then medical, dental, emotional, geothermal, statistical, a single lesion, and finally any pressurised fluid.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保留同一个动作：被关在里面的东西破壳而出。这个事件先是火山的，然后是医学的、牙齿的、情绪的、地热的、数量上的，再到单个病灶，最后是任何受压流体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed layer splitting and material shooting upward and outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：封闭的岩层裂开，物质向上向外冲出。

branches.en: PRESSURISED MATERIAL: magma, hot water and steam all escape through an opening.
branches.cn: 受压物质：岩浆、热水与蒸汽都通过开口逸出。

branches.en: SKIN: the mass outbreak and the single spot are two scales of the same medical event.
branches.cn: 皮肤：整体暴发与单个斑点，是同一医学事件的两种尺度。

branches.en: TEETH: a hard object physically breaks through soft tissue.
branches.cn: 牙齿：坚硬之物确实顶破柔软组织。

branches.en: FEELING: what was contained breaks out as anger or laughter.
branches.cn: 情绪：被压住的感受以愤怒或笑声冲出。

branches.en: QUANTITY: praise or data arrives suddenly and in bulk.
branches.cn: 数量：赞誉或数据突然且成批地到来。

intro.en: Eruption is a Latin noun of action: a prefix meaning out, a breaking stem, and a noun suffix, all three visible in the English word.
intro.cn: eruption 是拉丁动作名词：一个表示「出」的前缀、一个表示「破」的词干、一个名词后缀，三者都保留在英语词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin rumpere, erumpere, eruptio and eruptus give eruption, erupt, eruptive, rupture, interrupt, corrupt, abrupt and, through French and Italian, bankrupt.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rumpere、erumpere、eruptio 与 eruptus 衍生 eruption、erupt、eruptive、rupture、interrupt、corrupt、abrupt，并经法语与意大利语衍生 bankrupt。

items.example: The prefix e- marks movement out of a container.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 e- 标记离开容器的运动。

items.example: The stem rupt- carries the breaking in every word of the family.
items.exampleCN: 词干 rupt- 在词族的每个词里都承载「破」。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: Eruptio is the action noun built on the verb.
items.exampleCN: eruptio 是在动词之上构成的动作名词。

items.meaning: a breaking out; a bursting forth
items.example: The eruption began before dawn.
The seam erupted without warning.
items.exampleCN: 裂缝在毫无预警的情况下喷发。

items.example: The eruptive phase lasted three weeks.
The rupture in the pipe released steam.
items.exampleCN: 管道上的破裂释放出蒸汽。

items.example: A shout interrupted the reading.
The offer corrupted the clerk.
items.exampleCN: 这份好处使那名职员腐化。

items.example: The meeting came to an abrupt end.

items.structure: banca rotta (Italian, 'broken bench') via French, from Latin rupta
items.example: The firm went bankrupt that winter.
items.exampleCN: 那家公司在那个冬天破产了。

definition_zh: 逐步升级；不断加重；扩大
definition_en: to increase quickly in amount, intensity, or importance, or to cause something to do so
core_image: 楼梯一级一级往上，争执从低声耳语升到拍桌，再升到整层楼都能听见
scene: 价格压力使租金持续走高。Rents escalated through the year.
sceneCN: 这里 escalate 是「逐步上涨；升级」（第 1 个义项：数量或强度的逐级抬升）；句意：租金全年不断攀升。

pos.zh: 逐步升级；不断加重；扩大
使逐步升级；使逐步提高

derivatives.zh: 逐步升级；扩大
自动扶梯

senses.title: To climb step by step
senses.definition: to rise by successive stages in amount or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或程度上按连续阶段攀升
senses.example: Inflation escalated again.
senses.exampleCN: 通胀再度逐级上扬。
senses.why: The Latin stem is a ladder, so every rise is imagined as one more rung.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干是梯子，故每次上升都被想成多上一级横档。

senses.title: To intensify a confrontation
senses.definition: to make a dispute more serious, hostile, or dangerous than before
senses.definitionCN: 使争执比先前更严重、更敌对或更危险
senses.example: A remark escalated the quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 一句话使争吵升级。
senses.why: War reporting carried the verb from numbers into violence, where each step narrows the way back.
senses.whyCN: 战地报道把动词从数字带入暴力，每一步都让回头路更窄。

senses.title: To keep prices rising
senses.definition: to push costs or demands upward without a clear ceiling
senses.definitionCN: 把成本或要价推向没有明显上限的高处
senses.example: Bidding escalated the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 竞价使成交价一路走高。
senses.why: Commerce borrowed the climbing image for figures that refuse to settle.
senses.whyCN: 商界借这一攀升意象形容不肯落定的数字。

intro.en: Escalate is a back-formation from escalator, whose Latin source scala means ladder.
intro.cn: escalate 是从 escalator 逆推出来的词，其拉丁源头 scala 意为梯子。

items.en: Scala means ladder, and scandere to climb.
items.cn: scala 表梯子，scandere 表攀登。

items.en: Scala names military steps taken one after another.
items.cn: 十九世纪 scala 指军事上逐级采取的步骤。

items.en: Escalator is fixed for the moving stair in buildings.
items.cn: 二十世纪三十年代 escalator 专指楼宇中的移动楼梯。

items.en: Reporters coin escalate for a war that grows stage by stage.
items.cn: 朝鲜战争时期记者为生阶段扩大的战争造出 escalate。

items.en: The verb spreads through policy and news copy.
items.cn: 越南战争时期该动词在政策与新闻中普及。

items.en: Business and medicine use it for any steep rise.
items.cn: 现代英语中商界与医学用它形容任何陡升。

note.en: Group one holds the scala climbing family; group two holds other verbs of increasing.
note.cn: 第一组是 scala 这一表攀登的词族；第二组是其他表增加的动词。

entries.definition: The process or fact of escalating, common in policy writing.
entries.definitionCN: 升级的过程或事实，政策写作常用。

entries.definition: The everyday word for going upward by steps.
One who expounds, from Latin exponere, to take out.
entries.definitionCN: 阐述者，出自拉丁语 exponere「取出」。

entries.definition: To climb beyond a limit.
To increase force or strength without implying stages.
entries.definitionCN: 增强力量，不含逐级之义。

entries.definition: To worsen a condition or problem.
To rise or gather in growing amounts.
To move upward in a turning course that no one checks.
entries.definitionCN: 沿失控的旋势一路抬升。

normalIntro.en: Escalate is about stages; intensify is about force.
normalIntro.cn: escalate 关乎逐级台阶，intensify 关乎力度强弱。

normal.en: It takes an object in the causal use: escalate prices.
normal.cn: 使动用法带宾语：escalate prices。

normal.en: Follow with into for a new stage: escalate into war.
normal.cn: 接 into 表进入新阶段：escalate into war。

normal.en: Escalation is the rarer noun; avoid escalment.
normal.cn: 名词用 escalation，勿造 escalment。

normal.en: News pairs it with tensions, costs, rhetoric.
normal.cn: 新闻里常与 tensions、costs、rhetoric 搭配。

normal.en: It is neutral in form but negative in effect.
normal.cn: 形式中性，所指多为坏事。

abstract.en: Picture a stair lighted one step at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一级一级亮起来的楼梯灯。

abstract.en: Imagine an argument where each reply raises the voice another notch.
abstract.cn: 想象一场每答一句音量就再高一档的争论。

abstract.en: Think of an auction paddle passing row after row.
abstract.cn: 想想拍卖牌一排一排举起来。

examples.en: Disagreement escalated into a formal complaint.
examples.cn: 分歧升级为正式投诉。

examples.en: Fees escalated faster than wages.
examples.cn: 费用涨得比工资更快。

examples.en: Nobody planned how quickly the fight would escalate.
examples.cn: 没人料到冲突会如此迅速地升级。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一路看累他」——一路往上看得人发累，所以 escalate 是逐级升高、不断升级；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 scandere（攀登）→ scala（梯子）→ 英语 escalator（自动扶梯）→ 逆构动词 escalate，核心义「像上梯子一样一级一级抬高」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb covers plain rises, worsening conflicts, and climbing costs.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词涵盖普通的上涨、恶化的冲突与攀升的成本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ladder with another rung always above.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架梯子，总有一级横档在高处等着。

branches.en: Numbers move up in visible stages.
branches.cn: 数字以可见的阶段上移。

branches.en: Hostility climbs past the point of return.
branches.cn: 敌意爬过无法回头的节点。

branches.en: Prices rise because bidders keep stepping.
branches.cn: 出价者不断加码，价格随之上抬。

branches.en: Both measure a series of larger figures.
branches.cn: 两者都计量一串更大的数字。

branches.en: Both carry the sense of losing control.
branches.cn: 两者都含失控之感。

intro.en: A climbing stem, a ladder noun, and an English verbal ending meet in a back-formed verb.
intro.cn: 表攀登的词干、表梯子的名词与英语动词词尾在一个逆构动词里相遇。

latinIntro.en: Latin scandere is to climb, scala a ladder, and ascensus a rising.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scandere 表攀登，scala 表梯子，ascensus 表上升之事。

items.example: E- opens the climbing word.
Scal is the ladder inside.
The ending makes the verb.
Frequent in news past tense.
Used before costs and tensions.
The noun came before the verb.
Policy papers list escalation risks.
items.exampleCN: 政策文件列举升级风险。

items.example: Trans- carries the climb past a limit.

definition_zh: 自动扶梯；自动调整条款；自动上升通道
definition_en: a moving staircase that carries standing passengers between floors, or a mechanism that raises wages and prices by itself
core_image: 一条自己会走的楼梯，站着不动就被送到上一层
scene: 商场中庭里，人们站上一条自己会移动的楼梯，从一层被送到二层。Shoppers stood on the escalator and were carried up to the second floor.
sceneCN: 这里 escalator 是「自动扶梯」（第 1 个义项：会自己移动的楼梯）；句意：购物者站在自动扶梯上，被送到二层。

pos.zh: 自动扶梯；自动上升通道

derivatives.zh: 由 escalator 逆构而成，去掉 -or 后表示「逐步升级、不断加剧」
escalate 加名词后缀 -ion，指冲突或价格的逐步升级
escalate 加形容词后缀 -ory，指具有升级性质的

senses.title: A moving staircase
senses.definition: a mechanical staircase whose steps move continuously and carry people from one floor to another
senses.definitionCN: 梯级连续移动、把人们从一层送到另一层的机械楼梯
senses.example: The escalator was crowded after the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会散场后，自动扶梯上挤满了人。
senses.why: The word was coined in 1900 from the climbing stem of escalade plus the -or of elevator, so it names a machine that does the climbing for the rider.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在二十世纪初用 escalade 的「攀爬」词干加上 elevator 的 -or 造出，所以它指的是替乘客完成攀爬的机器。

senses.title: An automatic adjustment clause
senses.definition: a contract term or economic device that raises wages, prices, or fees automatically when a chosen index rises
senses.definitionCN: 当选定指数上升时自动提高工资、价格或费用的合同条款或经济机制
senses.example: The union won an escalator that ties pay to inflation.
senses.exampleCN: 工会争取到一条把工资与通胀挂钩的自动调整条款。
senses.why: Since the machine lifts people without any effort of their own, the same noun was borrowed for arrangements that lift pay or prices by themselves.
senses.whyCN: 既然这种机器不用人费力就能把人抬高，同一个名词就被借去指那些自行抬高工资或价格的安排。

senses.title: An effortless upward path
senses.definition: a route or process that lifts people or things upward without visible effort
senses.definitionCN: 让人或事物不费力气就向上走的路径或过程
senses.example: For many graduates, a degree was once an escalator into the middle class.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多毕业生来说，文凭一度是通往中产阶层的自动上升通道。
senses.why: The literal picture of a stair that moves by itself was extended to any smooth path of social or economic ascent.
senses.whyCN: 会自己移动的楼梯这一具体画面，被引申为任何顺畅的社会或经济上升路径。

intro.en: Escalator is a coined trademark name, built on the Latin ladder root with the -or ending of elevator.
intro.cn: escalator 是一个人造的商标名，用拉丁语「梯子」词根加上 elevator 的 -or 结尾构成。

items.en: Scandere means to climb, and it supplies the oldest layer of the word.
items.cn: scandere 意为攀登，是这个词最古老的一层。

items.en: Scala, plural scalae, means a ladder or a flight of steps.
items.cn: scala（复数 scalae）意为梯子或一段台阶。

items.en: Escalade names a ladder assault on a wall, from Italian scalata.
items.cn: escalade 指用云梯攻打城墙，来自意大利语 scalata。

items.en: Escalade enters English as a military term for climbing a fortification.
items.cn: escalade 在十六世纪进入英语，是攀登防御工事的军事术语。

items.en: In 1900 the Otis company coins escalator as a trademark for a moving stair, modelled on elevator.
items.cn: 一九〇〇年，奥的斯公司仿照 elevator 造出 escalator，作为移动楼梯的商标。

items.en: The verb escalate is back-formed from the noun in the 1920s, and the trademark later becomes a common noun.
items.cn: 动词 escalate 在二十世纪二十年代由这个名词逆构而成，商标后来也变成了普通名词。

note.en: Escalator belongs to the Latin ladder family of escalate and escalade, and in meaning it sits beside the words for lifts and stairs.
note.cn: escalator 属于拉丁语「梯子」词族的 escalate 与 escalade，在意义上与表示电梯、楼梯的词相邻。

entries.definition: to become greater, more serious, or more intense by stages
the act of climbing a wall with ladders in an attack
entries.definitionCN: 用云梯攀墙攻城的行动

entries.definition: to climb up something steep
entries.definitionCN: 攀上陡峭之物（这一动词与「梯子」同源；「规模」「鳞片」等义只是同形，来源不同）

entries.definition: a box-like machine that carries people up and down inside a building
entries.definitionCN: 在楼内上下运送人的箱式电梯（美式说法）

entries.definition: the British word for an elevator
a flat moving belt that carries people along a level or gently sloping passage
entries.definitionCN: 沿水平或缓坡通道运送人的平面移动步道

normalIntro.en: Escalator is a trademark name built from the climbing stem and the -or of elevator, and it later gave birth to the verb escalate.
normalIntro.cn: escalator 是用「攀爬」词干加 elevator 的 -or 造出的商标名，后来又反过来生出动词 escalate。

normal.en: The same stem gives escalate, which means to rise step by step.
normal.cn: 同一词干给出 escalate，意为一步一步地上升。

normal.en: The word began as a trademark of the Otis company around 1900.
normal.cn: 这个词大约在一九〇〇年作为奥的斯公司的商标出现。

normal.en: You can take the escalator or ride an escalator; both collocations are common.
normal.cn: 乘扶梯可以说「take the escalator」或「ride an escalator」，两种搭配都很常见。

normal.en: An escalator clause raises pay by itself when the index rises.
normal.cn: 自动调整条款在指数上升时自行提高工资。

normal.en: Compare elevator: a box that lifts you, while an escalator is a stair that moves.
normal.cn: 对比 elevator：它是把您抬起来的箱子，而扶梯是自己会动的楼梯。

abstract.en: Picture yourself standing still on a stair while the steps slide upward under your feet.
abstract.cn: 想象你站在楼梯上不动，脚下的梯级却自己往上滑。

abstract.en: Imagine a wage figure climbing on its own as soon as the price index moves.
abstract.cn: 想象工资数字在物价指数一动时自己往上爬。

abstract.en: Think of a hidden ramp inside society that lifts a whole class without any visible push.
abstract.cn: 想象社会内部有一条看不见的坡道，不用谁推就把整个阶层抬上去。

examples.en: She took the escalator instead of waiting for the lift.
examples.cn: 她没有等电梯，而是走了自动扶梯。

examples.en: A long escalator rises through the museum atrium.
examples.cn: 一条长长的自动扶梯穿过博物馆的中庭向上延伸。

examples.en: For a talented student, the scholarship acted as an escalator into a better life.
examples.cn: 对一个有天赋的学生来说，奖学金成了通往更好生活的上升通道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「es + calator」——后半截读起来像「客累特」，客人走累了就站上自动扶梯；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 scandere（攀登）→ scala（梯子、台阶）→ 法语 escalade（云梯攻城）→ 现代英语仿 elevator 造出 escalator（一九〇〇年商标），核心义「一级一级往上走」。

sensesIntro.en: Escalator begins as the name of the moving stair, then lends itself to automatic adjustment clauses, and finally becomes a metaphor for effortless ascent.
sensesIntro.cn: escalator 先是会动的楼梯的名字，随后被借去指自动调整条款，最后成为「不费力上升」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase that moves by itself and lifts a rider who never takes a step.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条自己会动的楼梯，把站着不动的人送上去。

branches.en: The machine itself is the first and central sense.
branches.cn: 机器本身是第一层、也是中心的义项。

branches.en: The clause sense borrows the automatic lift for wages and prices.
branches.cn: 条款义把这种自动抬升借给了工资和价格。

branches.en: The metaphorical sense turns the machine into an image of effortless ascent.
branches.cn: 比喻义把机器变成了不费力上升的形象。

branches.en: Both rest on the idea of rising without a deliberate step.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在「不必刻意迈步就能上升」这一观念上。

branches.en: Both are figurative offshoots of the machine, one economic and one social.
branches.cn: 两者都是机器义衍生出的比喻，一个属经济，一个属社会。

intro.en: Escalator is built from the Latin ladder root and the -or ending of elevator, and English keeps a whole family around it.
intro.cn: escalator 由拉丁语「梯子」词根与 elevator 的 -or 结尾构成，英语围绕它保留了一整族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin scandere means to climb, and scala means a ladder or steps; both feed the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scandere 意为攀登，scala 意为梯子或台阶，两者共同哺育了这个英语词。

items.example: Scandere is the oldest root behind the word.
items.exampleCN: scandere 是这个词背后最古老的词根。

items.meaning: a ladder, a flight of steps
items.example: Scala gives the stair image its name.
items.exampleCN: scala 为楼梯这一意象提供了名字。

items.example: Scalaris shows the adjective built on scala.
items.exampleCN: scalaris 展示了由 scala 构成的形容词。

items.example: Escalade keeps the climbing sense alive in English.
items.exampleCN: escalade 在英语里保留着攀爬的含义。

items.meaning: one who or that which does
items.meaningCN: 表示施动者或工具的结尾
items.example: The suffix -or turns a stem into a machine name.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 把词干变成机器名称。

items.example: Escalate was formed from the noun.
items.exampleCN: escalate 是由这个名词逆构出来的。

items.example: Escalation names the process of rising.
Elevator supplied the -or ending.
items.exampleCN: elevator 提供了 -or 这个结尾。

items.example: Escalator became a common noun after its trademark years.
items.exampleCN: escalator 在商标年代之后变成了普通名词。

definition_zh: 尤其；特别；专门地
definition_en: more than usual, or for one particular purpose
core_image: 一群人中有一张脸被聚光灯单独照亮
scene: 考前复习时，他尤其重视错题，反复看那些容易出错的题。When reviewing before the exam, he paid special attention to mistakes, especially the questions he often got wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 especially 是「尤其」（第 1 个义项：在同类中格外突出）；句意：考前复习时，他尤其重视错题，反复看那些容易出错的题。

derivatives.zh: 特别的
特别的
特意地

senses.title: More than usual
senses.definition: more than usual or more than others
senses.definitionCN: 比通常或比其他人更突出
senses.example: The streets are busy, especially on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 街上很热闹，尤其是周末。
senses.why: The word marks one member of a group as standing out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把群体中的某一员标为格外突出。

senses.title: For a particular purpose
senses.definition: for one particular purpose rather than in general
senses.definitionCN: 为某个特定目的而非一般用途
senses.example: This tool is especially designed for small hands.
senses.exampleCN: 这件工具是专门为小手设计的。
senses.why: Singling out one purpose is another way of making something special.
senses.whyCN: 单独挑出一个目的，是让某事物特别的另一种方式。

intro.en: Especially is especial plus -ly, from Latin specialis, belonging to a kind.
intro.cn: especially 由 especial 加 -ly 构成，源自拉丁语 specialis（属于某一类的）。

items.en: Species means a kind or appearance.
items.cn: species 意为种类或外观。

items.en: Specialis means belonging to a particular kind.
items.cn: specialis 意为属于特定种类的。

items.en: Especial enters French with the sense of special.
items.cn: especial 以「特别的」含义进入法语。

items.en: Especial means distinguished from others.
items.cn: especial 意为从其他事物中突出。

items.en: Especially marks a standout case or purpose.
items.cn: especially 标记突出的情况或目的。

note.en: Especially is close to particularly and specially.
note.cn: especially 与 particularly、specially 相近。

entries.definition: special
not ordinary
for a particular purpose
especially, more than usual
more than anything else
especially, in a way worth noticing

normalIntro.en: Especially puts a spotlight on one item in a group.
normalIntro.cn: especially 就像把聚光灯打在群体中的某一项上。

normal.en: Especially important means more important than the rest.
normal.cn: especially important 意为比其余的更重要的。

normal.en: Especially for children means mostly aimed at them.
normal.cn: especially for children 意为主要针对孩子。

normal.en: Not especially means only a little or not very.
normal.cn: not especially 意为并不太。

normal.en: The adjective is especial, though special is more common.
normal.cn: 形容词是 especial，不过 special 更常用。

normal.en: Compare specially: specially means for a purpose, especially means above all.
normal.cn: 对比 specially：specially 意为专门地，especially 意为尤其。

abstract.en: Picture one bright star in a dark sky.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗天空中一颗格外明亮的星。

abstract.en: Imagine one voice rising above a choir.
abstract.cn: 想象合唱中一个声音高过其他声音。

abstract.en: Think of a page with one word circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上有一个词被红笔圈出。

examples.en: I love fruit, especially peaches.
examples.cn: 我喜欢水果，尤其是桃子。

examples.en: The roads are dangerous, especially at night.
examples.cn: 这些路很危险，尤其是在夜里。

examples.en: This course is especially useful for beginners.
examples.cn: 这门课对初学者特别有用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（外）＋ special（特别）＋ ly」——从普通中特别挑出来，就是尤其；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 species（种类）→ specialis（属于某类的）→ 古法语 especial → especial ＋ -ly → especially，核心义「从同类中格外突出」。

sensesIntro.en: Especially first marks something as more than usual, and then marks a special purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: especially 先把某事物标为格外突出，再标记特定目的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one face lit by a spotlight in a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中一张被聚光灯照亮的脸。

branches.en: One member stands out above the rest.
branches.cn: 其中一员比其他成员更突出。

branches.en: The word can also mark a special purpose.
branches.cn: 这个词也能标记特殊目的。

branches.en: A standout item often serves a standout use.
branches.cn: 突出的东西往往有突出的用途。

branches.en: Emphasis is the main job of the word.
branches.cn: 强调是这个词的主要功能。

branches.en: A tool made for one job is especially designed.
branches.cn: 为一项工作特制的工具就是专门设计的。

intro.en: Especially adds the adverb ending -ly to especial, which shares a root with special.
intro.cn: especially 在 especial 后加副词词尾 -ly，而 especial 与 special 同根。

latinIntro.en: Latin species, a kind, gives specialis and the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 species（种类）衍生出 specialis 及整个词族。

items.example: Species supplies the idea of a kind.
Specialis marks what belongs to a kind.
items.exampleCN: specialis 标记属于某类的事物。

items.example: Especial is the adjective base.
The suffix -ly forms especially.
Especially marks the standout case.
Special is the common shorter form.
items.exampleCN: special 是常用的较短形式。

items.example: Specially marks purpose rather than degree.
items.exampleCN: specially 标记目的而非程度。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms specialist.
A specialist knows one field deeply.
items.exampleCN: specialist 深入掌握某一领域。

definition_zh: 文章；短文；随笔
definition_en: a short piece of writing about a subject
core_image: 一叠写满字的纸，第一页写着标题和观点
scene: 老师让我们写一篇关于城市生活的短文，下周一交。The teacher asked us to write an essay about city life and hand it in next Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 essay 是「短文」（第 1 个义项：围绕一个主题写的短篇文章）；句意：老师让我们写一篇关于城市生活的短文，下周一交。

derivatives.zh: 随笔作家
随笔风格的

senses.title: A short piece of writing
senses.definition: a short piece of writing that gives the writer's ideas on a subject
senses.definitionCN: 就某一主题表达作者观点的短篇文章
senses.example: She wrote an essay on modern art.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了一篇关于现代艺术的文章。
senses.why: The French source means an attempt, so an essay is an attempt to put ideas into words.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为尝试，因此文章就是把想法写成文字的尝试。

senses.title: An attempt
senses.definition: an attempt to do something, used in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的尝试，用于正式书面语
senses.example: His first essay in politics ended in failure.
senses.exampleCN: 他初次尝试政治以失败告终。
senses.why: The older sense of a trial attempt still appears in formal English.
senses.whyCN: 「尝试」这一古老含义仍出现在正式英语中。

intro.en: Essay comes from French essai, a trial, from Latin exigere, to weigh or test.
intro.cn: essay 源自法语 essai（尝试），源自拉丁语 exigere（称量、检验）。

items.en: Exigere means to weigh or examine.
items.cn: exigere 意为称量或检验。

items.en: Essai means a trial or attempt.
items.cn: essai 意为尝试或试验。

items.en: Montaigne's essays make the word famous.
items.cn: 蒙田的随笔让这个词广为人知。

items.en: Essay means a short written composition.
items.cn: essay 指短篇书面作品。

items.en: School essays are a common use.
items.cn: 学校作文是常见用法。

note.en: Essay is close to article and paper, but usually shorter and personal.
note.cn: essay 与文章、论文相近，但通常更短、更具个人色彩。

entries.definition: a writer of essays
like an essay
a test of metal or quality
a piece of writing in a newspaper
a long academic piece of writing
a piece of writing done as school work

normalIntro.en: An essay is an attempt with a pen: you try out your ideas on paper.
normalIntro.cn: essay 是一次用笔的尝试：在纸上试验自己的想法。

normal.en: Write an essay means produce a short paper.
normal.cn: write an essay 意为写一篇短文。

normal.en: An essay question asks for discussion, not a single word.
normal.cn: essay question 要求论述，而不是一个单词。

normal.en: An essay on a subject is written about it.
normal.cn: an essay on a subject 是就某主题写的文章。

normal.en: An essayist writes essays as a craft.
normal.cn: essayist 以写随笔为业。

normal.en: Compare article: an article is published, an essay may be for class.
normal.cn: 对比 article：article 多指发表的文章，essay 可以是为课堂写的。

abstract.en: Picture a blank page slowly filling with neat lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一页白纸渐渐写满整齐的字行。

abstract.en: Imagine a title at the top and one clear idea below.
abstract.cn: 想象顶端一个标题，下面一个清晰的观点。

abstract.en: Think of a writer testing an idea like a small experiment.
abstract.cn: 想象作家像做小实验一样检验一个想法。

examples.en: He handed in his essay two days late.
examples.cn: 他晚了两天交文章。

examples.en: The essay won first prize in the contest.
examples.cn: 这篇文章在比赛中获得一等奖。

examples.en: Her essay on friendship is easy to read.
examples.cn: 她写友情的文章读起来很轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「essay」听起来像「爱写」——爱写的人常写短文，这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 exigere（称量、检验）→ 法语 essai（尝试）→ essay，核心义「对想法的文字试验」。

sensesIntro.en: Essay first means a short written work, and retains an older formal sense of an attempt.
sensesIntro.cn: essay 先指短篇文字作品，并保留「尝试」这一较古老的正式含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page filled with a title and a line of argument.
core.cn: 核心意象：写有标题与论点的一页纸。

branches.en: A short composition is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 短篇文章是日常义项。

branches.en: The old sense of an attempt survives in formal use.
branches.cn: 「尝试」的旧义在正式用法中保留。

branches.en: School and exams make the word common.

branches.cn: 文章有主题、观点与结论。

items.example: Ex- appears in the Latin source.

definition_zh: 本质；实质；精华；香精
definition_en: the basic nature of something, its most important quality, or a concentrated extract used for flavour or scent
core_image: 一层层剥掉外壳后，剩下的那一小滴最浓的东西
scene: 调香师把一大筐花瓣倒进蒸馏器，最后瓶底只留下一小滴香气最浓的液体。The perfumer distilled a basket of petals and kept a few drops of essence.
sceneCN: 这里 essence 是「香精、精华」（第 3 个义项：从植物中提取的浓缩液）；句意：调香师蒸馏了一筐花瓣，只留下几滴香精。

derivatives.zh: essence 加形容词后缀 -ial，指「本质的；必不可少的」
essential 加副词后缀 -ly，指「本质上；基本上」
quint-（第五）加 essence 构成，指「精华；典范」，源出炼金术的第五元素

senses.title: The intrinsic nature of a thing
senses.definition: the set of qualities that make a thing what it is and not something else
senses.definitionCN: 使一事物成为该事物、而不是别的事物的那些根本性质
senses.example: Philosophers asked what the essence of a human being might be.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问人的本质究竟是什么。
senses.why: Cicero coined Latin essentia from the verb esse, to be, so the word names the being of a thing rather than its surface.
senses.whyCN: 西塞罗用动词 esse（是、存在）造出拉丁语 essentia，因此这个词命名的是事物的「存在本身」，而不是它的表面。

senses.title: The central point of something said or made
senses.definition: the most important idea or quality of something, especially when it can be put briefly
senses.definitionCN: 某事物最重要的想法或品质，尤指可以简短说出来的那部分
senses.example: The essence of her argument is that speed has a cost.
senses.exampleCN: 她论点的核心是：速度是有代价的。
senses.why: If essence is what a thing is, then the essence of a speech or a plan is the part without which it would no longer be itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然 essence 指一物之所是，那么一段讲话或一个计划的「essence」，就是缺了它便不再是它自己的那部分。

senses.title: A concentrated extract
senses.definition: a strong liquid drawn from a plant or food, used to give flavour or scent
senses.definitionCN: 从植物或食物中提取的浓液，用来提供味道或香气
senses.example: Add a few drops of vanilla essence to the cake mixture.
senses.exampleCN: 往蛋糕糊里加几滴香草香精。
senses.why: Alchemists spoke of a quinta essentia, a fifth and purest element, and from that idea the word came to name the purified concentrate of a substance.
senses.whyCN: 炼金术士讲「quinta essentia」，即第五种、最纯的元素；从这个观念出发，这个词开始指物质被提纯后的浓缩部分。

intro.en: Essence comes from Latin essentia, a philosophical coinage by Cicero rendering Greek ousia, built on the verb esse, to be.
intro.cn: essence 来自拉丁语 essentia，这是西塞罗为翻译希腊语 ousia 而造出的哲学术语，根基是动词 esse（是、存在）。

items.en: Esse means to be, and it is the base of the whole family.
items.cn: esse 意为「是、存在」，是这一整族词的根基。

items.en: Cicero coins essentia to render the Greek word ousia, the being of a thing.
items.cn: 西塞罗造出 essentia，用来翻译希腊语 ousia，即事物的「存在」。

items.en: The ending -entia forms abstract nouns of state, as in prudentia and patientia.
items.cn: 词尾 -entia 构成表示状态的名词，如 prudentia 与 patientia。

items.en: Essence carries the philosophical noun into French.
items.cn: essence 把这个哲学名词带入法语。

items.en: Essence appears in English in the fourteenth century, first in philosophical writing.
items.cn: essence 在十四世纪进入英语，最早出现在哲学写作中。

items.en: From the idea of a quinta essentia, the purest fifth element, the word later names concentrated flavourings and scents.
items.cn: 由「第五元素」quinta essentia 的观念出发，这个词后来指浓缩的调味液与香气。

note.en: Essence is the noun of being, close in form to essential and quintessence and in meaning to nature, substance, and extract.
note.cn: essence 是表示「存在」的名词，形式上与 essential、quintessence 相近，意义上与 nature、substance、extract 相邻。

entries.definition: absolutely necessary, or relating to the inner nature of something
entries.definitionCN: 必不可少的；与内在本质有关的

entries.definition: in basic nature, when everything else is stripped away
the purest and most perfect example of a quality
entries.definitionCN: 某品质最纯粹、最完美的体现（由拉丁语「第五元素」构成）

entries.definition: the usual character of a person or thing
entries.definitionCN: 人或事物通常具有的特性

entries.definition: the real matter or the most important content of something
entries.definitionCN: 某物的实体或其最重要的内容

entries.definition: a concentrated substance taken out of a plant or food
entries.definitionCN: 从植物或食物中提取出的浓缩物

normalIntro.en: Essence is the noun of being: it comes from esse, and the whole family of essential and quintessence grows from it.
normalIntro.cn: essence 是表示「存在」的名词，来自 esse，essential 与 quintessence 这一族词都从它长出来。

normal.en: The verb esse, to be, is the root of essence, essential, and essentially.
normal.cn: 动词 esse（是、存在）是 essence、essential 与 essentially 的根。

normal.en: Quintessence is quinta essentia, the fifth and purest element of the alchemists.
normal.cn: quintessence 即「quinta essentia」，是炼金术士所说的第五种、最纯的元素。

normal.en: In essence means in its basic nature, once details are set aside.
normal.cn: 「in essence」意为本质上，即把细节放到一边之后。

normal.en: If something is of the essence, it is absolutely necessary.
normal.cn: 如果某事「of the essence」，那就是绝对不可缺少的。

normal.en: Compare nature and substance: nature is how a thing behaves, substance is what it is made of.
normal.cn: 对比 nature 与 substance：nature 是事物的表现方式，substance 是它由什么构成。

abstract.en: Picture peeling an onion layer by layer until only a tiny core is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一层层剥开洋葱，最后只剩下一小颗核心。

abstract.en: Imagine a long speech being boiled down to one short sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一段很长的讲话被熬成一句很短的话。

abstract.en: Think of a hundred roses squeezed into one small bottle of oil.
abstract.cn: 想象一百朵玫瑰被压进一小瓶精油里。

examples.en: The essence of the treaty is a promise not to attack.
examples.cn: 这份条约的实质是承诺不发动攻击。

examples.en: She added a few drops of essence to the cream.
examples.cn: 她往奶油里加了几滴香精。

examples.en: In a rescue like this, time is of the essence.
examples.cn: 在这样的救援中，时间至关重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「es + sence」——后半截像「sense」（感觉），把一层层感觉剥掉，剩下的才是本质；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 esse（是、存在）→ 西塞罗仿希腊语 ousia 造出 essentia（本质）→ 古法语 essence → 英语 essence，核心义「使一物成为该物的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Essence begins as the philosophical being of a thing, narrows to the central point of a statement, and widens again to a purified concentrate.
sensesIntro.cn: essence 先是事物在哲学意义上的「存在」，再收窄为一段话的要点，最后又扩展为被提纯的浓缩物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the small pure drop that remains after everything else is boiled away.
core.cn: 核心意象：把别的东西都熬掉之后，剩下的那一小滴纯净物。

branches.en: The philosophical sense names what makes a thing what it is.
branches.cn: 哲学义命名的是使一物成为该物的东西。

branches.en: The central-point sense applies that inner core to words and plans.
branches.cn: 要点义把这个内在核心用到言辞和计划上。

branches.en: The extract sense makes the core something physical and concentrated.
branches.cn: 提取物义把这个核心变成可触摸的浓缩物。

branches.en: Both answer the question of what something really is once details are removed.
branches.cn: 两者都在回答：去掉细节之后，某物究竟是什么。

branches.en: Both point to a purified core, one abstract and one chemical.
branches.cn: 两者都指向被提纯的核心，一个抽象，一个物质。

intro.en: Essence belongs to the Latin verb esse, to be, and English builds essential, essentially, and quintessence on the same stem.
intro.cn: essence 属于拉丁语动词 esse（是、存在）一族，英语在同一词干上构成 essential、essentially 与 quintessence。

latinIntro.en: Latin esse means to be; essentia, coined by Cicero, means the being of a thing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 esse 意为「是、存在」；西塞罗造出的 essentia 意为事物的存在。

items.example: Esse is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: esse 是这一族词的基础动词。

items.example: Essentia was the coinage of Cicero for Greek ousia.
items.exampleCN: essentia 是西塞罗为希腊语 ousia 造的译名。

items.example: The suffix -entia turns a stem into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -entia 把词干变成抽象名词。

items.example: Essence keeps the philosophical sense.
Essential is the adjective of the same stem.
items.exampleCN: essential 是同词干的形容词。

items.example: Essentially adds the adverb ending.

items.meaning: the fifth essence, the purest part
items.example: Quintessence joins quinta to essentia.
items.exampleCN: quintessence 把 quinta 与 essentia 组合起来。

items.example: Quinta essentia named the purest element above fire, air, water, and earth.
items.exampleCN: quinta essentia 指火、气、水、土之上最纯的元素。

items.meaning: the view that things have fixed essences
items.meaningCN: 认为事物具有固定本质的学说
items.example: Essentialism extends the noun into philosophy.
items.exampleCN: essentialism 把这个名词延伸到哲学。

definition_zh: 必不可少的；本质的；要素
definition_en: completely necessary, or forming the basic nature of something
core_image: 一座桥最关键的那块基石，抽掉它整座桥就会塌
scene: 水对所有的生物都是必不可少的，没有它谁也活不了。Water is essential to all living things, and nothing can survive without it.
sceneCN: 这里 essential 是「必不可少的」（第 1 个义项：缺了就完全无法维持）；句意：水对所有的生物都是必不可少的，没有它谁也活不了。

derivatives.zh: 本质上；基本上
本质；精髓

senses.title: Completely necessary
senses.definition: so important that something cannot work without it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到没有它就无法运作
senses.example: Sleep is essential for good health.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠对健康必不可少。
senses.why: The word comes from essence, so what is essential belongs to the very being of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 essence，因此 essential 指属于事物存在本身的东西。

senses.title: Forming the basic nature
senses.definition: forming the central nature of something
senses.definitionCN: 构成某事物的核心性质
senses.example: Freedom is an essential feature of democracy.
senses.exampleCN: 自由是民主的本质特征。
senses.why: The basic nature of a thing is what cannot be removed without changing it.
senses.whyCN: 事物的本质就是抽掉后它就不再是它自己的东西。

senses.title: A basic necessary thing
senses.definition: something that is completely necessary
senses.definitionCN: 完全不可缺少的事物
senses.example: The guide covers the essentials of camping.
senses.exampleCN: 这本指南涵盖了露营的基本要点。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the necessary things themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，指那些必要的事物本身。

intro.en: Essential comes from Late Latin essentialis, from essentia, being or nature.
intro.cn: essential 源自晚期拉丁语 essentialis，来自 essentia（存在、本性）。

items.en: Essentia means being or nature.
items.cn: essentia 意为存在或本性。

items.en: Essentialis means belonging to the essence.
items.cn: essentialis 意为属于本质的。

items.en: Essential means forming the nature of something.
items.cn: essential 意为构成某事物的本性。

items.en: It also means absolutely necessary.
items.cn: 它也意为绝对必要。

items.en: The plural essentials names necessary items.
items.cn: 复数 essentials 指必需物品。

note.en: Essential is close to necessary and vital, and to essence in meaning.
note.cn: essential 与必要的、至关重要的相近，并与 essence 意义相连。

normal.cn: essential to health 意为没有它健康就会垮。

normal.en: An essential part is one you cannot remove.

normal.en: Absolutely essential means there is no substitute.

normal.en: The bare essentials are the smallest necessary set.

normal.en: Compare vital: vital stresses life, essential stresses necessity.

abstract.en: Picture the one stone that holds up an arch.
abstract.cn: 想象支撑整座拱门的那块石头。

abstract.en: Imagine a recipe missing its key ingredient.
abstract.cn: 想象一份缺少关键原料的食谱。

abstract.en: Think of a key that opens the only door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能打开唯一那扇门的钥匙。

examples.en: It is essential to book early.
examples.cn: 尽早预订是必不可少的。

examples.en: Trust is an essential part of friendship.
examples.cn: 信任是友谊的关键部分。

examples.en: Pack only the essentials for the trip.
examples.cn: 旅行只带必需品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「essence（本质）＋ ial」——属于本质的东西，就是必不可少的；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 essentia（存在、本性）→ 晚期拉丁语 essentialis → essential，核心义「属于事物本性、缺之不可」。

sensesIntro.en: Essential first means completely necessary, then belonging to the basic nature, and as a noun it names necessary things.
sensesIntro.cn: essential 先指完全必要，再指属于本质，作名词时指必需品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the keystone whose removal collapses the arch.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽掉就会让拱门倒塌的拱心石。

branches.en: Complete necessity is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 完全必要是日常义项。

branches.en: The basic nature of a thing is its essence.
branches.cn: 事物的基本性质就是它的本质。

branches.en: As a noun it names necessary items.
branches.cn: 作名词时指必需物品。

branches.en: What belongs to the essence is what cannot be removed.
branches.cn: 属于本质的东西就是不能抽掉的东西。

branches.en: The essentials of a subject are its core points.
branches.cn: 一门学科的 essentials 就是其核心要点。

intro.en: Essential adds -ial to essence, from Latin essentia.
intro.cn: essential 在 essence 上加 -ial，源自拉丁语 essentia。

latinIntro.en: Essentia comes from esse, to be, so essence is the very being of a thing.
latinIntro.cn: essentia 来自 esse（存在），因此本质就是事物的存在本身。

senses.whyCN: 说明某事物究竟是什么，就是把概念落到实际效果上。

items.en: Essentia means being or nature.

definition_zh: 尊重；敬重；好评；认为；视为
definition_en: to respect and value someone or something highly, or a feeling of high respect
core_image: 双手接过一件旧物，郑重地把它放到最高一层
scene: 毕业多年后，学生回到母校，把一本旧词典送还给老师。Years later, the student still holds the old teacher in high esteem.
