senses.title: High respect
senses.definition: a feeling of deep respect and approval for someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人怀有的深切敬意与认可
senses.example: The old coach is held in great esteem by his players.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老教练深受队员们的敬重。
senses.why: The Latin verb aestimare means to fix a value, so esteeming a person is setting a high value on that person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 aestimare 意为「估定价值」，所以敬重一个人就是给这个人定下很高的价值。

senses.title: Good opinion, standing
senses.definition: the good opinion that other people have of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 他人对某人或某物持有的好评与看重
senses.example: The school has risen in public esteem over the past decade.
senses.exampleCN: 过去十年间，这所学校在公众中的声誉提高了。
senses.why: Once a value has been assigned, the word can name the standing a person enjoys in the eyes of others.
senses.whyCN: 价值一经评定，这个词就转而指一个人在他人眼中的地位与声望。

senses.title: To regard as
senses.definition: to consider or judge something to be a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某事看作或判定为某种性质
senses.example: I esteem it a privilege to speak at this ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 我认为能在这场典礼上发言是一种荣幸。
senses.why: The old appraisal sense survives in the pattern esteem something as something, where the mind assigns a value or a label.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「估价」义保留在「esteem 某物为某物」的句式中：头脑给事物贴上价值或名目的标签。

senses.title: To appraise, to value
senses.definition: to judge the worth or amount of something, an older use
senses.definitionCN: 判断某物的价值或数量，属于较古的用法
senses.example: In old ledgers the land was esteemed at a modest sum.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧账簿里，这块地被估为一个不大的数目。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense of aestimare, a plain valuation, before the word narrowed to respect.
senses.whyCN: 这正是拉丁语 aestimare 的本义，平实的估价；后来词义才收窄为尊重。

intro.en: Esteem goes back to Latin aestimare, to value or appraise, through Old French estimer.
intro.cn: esteem 可追溯到拉丁语 aestimare（估价、评定价值），经古法语 estimer 进入英语。

items.en: Aestimare means to value or to appraise something.
items.cn: aestimare 意为给某物估价、评定价值。

items.en: Aestimatio names the act of valuation and the value set.
items.cn: aestimatio 指估价这一行为以及被定下的价值。

items.en: Estimer carries the verb into French with the sense of holding in regard.
items.cn: estimer 把动词带入法语，并带上「看重」的含义。

items.en: Estemen appears in English for valuing and for respecting.
items.cn: 中古英语 estemen 出现，兼有估价与尊重两义。

items.en: Modern English keeps esteem mainly as respect, while estimate takes over the counting sense.
items.cn: 现代英语里 esteem 主要保留尊重，而 estimate 接过了计量估价之义。

note.en: Esteem sits inside the Latin value family and beside the everyday words for respect.
note.cn: esteem 与拉丁语「估价」词族相连，也与日常表示尊重的词相邻。

entries.definition: worthy of respect
a judgement or opinion of value
respect for oneself
a feeling of admiration for someone
attention or respect for someone
a feeling of great approval

normalIntro.en: Esteem is a scale in the mind: a person is weighed and found valuable.
normalIntro.cn: esteem 是心里的一杆秤：把人称过之后，认定其价值很高。

normal.en: To hold someone in high esteem is to respect that person deeply.
normal.cn: hold someone in high esteem 就是深深敬重某人。

normal.en: Self-esteem is the value you place on yourself.
normal.cn: self-esteem 是你给自己定下的价值。

normal.en: A mark of esteem is a sign that others value you.
normal.cn: a mark of esteem 是别人看重你的表示。

normal.en: Esteem and estimate share one Latin root but have drifted apart.
normal.cn: esteem 与 estimate 同出一个拉丁词根，后来分道扬镳。

normal.en: The phrase esteem it a privilege keeps the old sense of judging something to be valuable.
normal.cn: esteem it a privilege 这个说法保留了「判定某物有价值」的古义。

abstract.en: Picture both hands receiving an old book and placing it on the top shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象双手接过一本旧书，把它放到书架最高一层。（对应第 1 个义项：把人放在心里的高处，就是敬重）

abstract.en: Imagine a name rising on a public list as neighbours nod in approval.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字在众人名单上往上走，邻居们纷纷点头称许。（对应第 2 个义项：声望就是别人眼中的位置）

abstract.en: Picture a judge setting a high price on a small object and calling it precious.
abstract.cn: 想象鉴定人给一件小物件定下高价，称它珍贵。（对应第 3 个义项：认为、视为就是给事物定名分）

examples.en: The students hold their teacher in high esteem.
examples.cn: 学生们非常敬重他们的老师。

examples.en: Her self-esteem grew after she finished the course.
examples.cn: 完成课程后，她的自尊心增强了。

examples.en: The village esteemed him as a fair judge.
examples.cn: 村里人把他视为公正的裁判。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一斯汀」——记成「一心一意把对方当尊长」，于是有敬重之意；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aestimare（估价、评定价值）→ aestimatio（评价）→ 古法语 estimer → 中古英语 estemen → 英语 esteem，核心义「给某人定下很高的价值」。

sensesIntro.en: Esteem starts as a valuation, becomes the respect a person commands, and keeps a formal verb sense of regarding something as valuable.
sensesIntro.cn: esteem 从估价出发，转为一个人赢得的敬重与声望，并保留「认为某物有价值」的正式动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of hands weighing something and setting it high.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手把某物掂量之后，放到高处。

branches.en: Respect is the value placed on a person.
branches.cn: 敬意是给一个人定下的价值。

branches.en: Public esteem is the standing others grant.
branches.cn: 声誉是他人给予的地位。

branches.en: To esteem as is to judge something to be valuable.
branches.cn: 认为、视为就是判定某物有价值。

branches.en: Both the noun and the verb keep the old valuation image.
branches.cn: 名词与动词都保留着古老的估价意象。

branches.en: A judgement repeated by many people hardens into public standing.
branches.cn: 许多人的判断反复叠加，就固化为公众声望。

intro.en: Esteem belongs to the Latin value family, and English builds estimable, estimation, and self-esteem around it.
intro.cn: esteem 属于拉丁语「估价」词族，英语围绕它构成 estimable、estimation 与 self-esteem。

latinIntro.en: Latin aestimare means to value, and aestimatio means a valuation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aestimare 意为估价，aestimatio 意为估价、评价。

items.example: Aestimare is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: aestimare 是整个词族的源头。

items.example: Aestimatio names the act of valuing.

items.meaning: to value, to hold in regard
items.example: Old French estimer carries both senses.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 estimer 兼有估价与看重两义。

items.example: Esteem keeps the noun sense of respect.
items.exampleCN: esteem 保留表示尊重的名词义。

items.example: The verb esteems a person or a plan.
items.exampleCN: 动词 esteem 可接人或计划作宾语。

items.example: The suffix -able forms estimable.
Estimable describes a person worth valuing.
items.exampleCN: estimable 形容值得看重的人。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms estimation.
Estimation moves toward judgement.
The prefix self- forms self-esteem.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 self- 构成 self-esteem。

items.example: Self-esteem is the value one places on oneself.
items.exampleCN: self-esteem 是自己给自己定下的价值。

definition_zh: 估计；估算；评价
definition_en: to guess the size, cost or value of something
core_image: 用眼睛和手比量，给出一串近似的数字
scene: 工程师估计这项工程还需要三个月才能完成。The engineers estimate that the project will need another three months.
sceneCN: 这里 estimate 是「估计」（第 1 个义项：根据现有信息推测数量或时间）；句意：工程师估计这项工程还需要三个月才能完成。

derivatives.zh: 估计；评价
估计的
高估

senses.title: Guess an amount
senses.definition: to calculate an amount roughly from available information
senses.definitionCN: 根据现有信息粗略计算数量
senses.example: We estimate the trip will take six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 我们估计这趟行程要六个小时。
senses.why: The Latin source means to value, so estimating puts a number on something uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为估价，因此 estimate 就是给不确定的事物一个数字。

senses.title: Judge worth
senses.definition: to form an opinion about someone's ability or character
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的能力或品格形成看法
senses.example: You should not estimate people by their clothes.
senses.exampleCN: 你不该凭衣着评价人。
senses.why: Valuing a thing and valuing a person use the same act of judgment.
senses.whyCN: 给东西估价与评价一个人，用的是同一种判断行为。

senses.title: A written price
senses.definition: a statement of how much work will cost
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项工作将花费多少钱的单据
senses.example: Ask the builder for an estimate first.
senses.exampleCN: 先向建筑商要一份报价。
senses.why: The noun is the number produced by estimating.
senses.whyCN: 名词就是估计之后得出的数字。

intro.en: Estimate comes from Latin aestimare, to value or judge.
intro.cn: estimate 源自拉丁语 aestimare（估价、判断）。

items.en: Aestimare means to value or rate.
items.cn: aestimare 意为估价或评定。

items.en: Aestimatio means a valuation.
items.cn: aestimatio 意为估价。

items.en: Estimate enters English as a verb and noun.
items.cn: estimate 以动词和名词形式进入英语。

items.en: It covers cost, time and size.
items.cn: 它涵盖成本、时间与规模。

items.en: A written estimate is a common business document.
items.cn: 书面报价是常见的商业文件。

note.en: Estimate is close to calculate and assess, and keeps the idea of value.
note.cn: estimate 与计算、评估相近，并保留「估价」的核心。

entries.definition: judgment or rough calculation
roughly calculated
to guess too high
to find a number by using math
to judge the quality or value of something
to give an answer without being sure

normalIntro.en: An estimate is a careful guess with a number attached.
normalIntro.cn: estimate 就是附上数字的谨慎猜测。

normal.en: Estimate the cost means work out roughly how much it will be.
normal.cn: estimate the cost 意为粗略算出要花多少钱。

normal.en: A rough estimate is not exact.
normal.cn: a rough estimate 并不精确。

normal.en: It is estimated that introduces a general calculation.
normal.cn: it is estimated that 引出大致的推算。

normal.en: A written estimate can be signed and accepted.
normal.cn: 书面报价可以签字接受。

normal.en: Compare calculate: calculate finds an exact number, estimate finds an approximate one.
normal.cn: 对比 calculate：calculate 求精确数字，estimate 求近似值。

abstract.en: Picture a hand measuring a table by eye.
abstract.cn: 想象用手凭眼力比量一张桌子。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale that stops between two marks.
abstract.cn: 想象天平停在两个刻度之间。

abstract.en: Think of a number written with a question mark beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字旁边画着问号。

examples.en: Experts estimate the damage at two million.
examples.cn: 专家估计损失为两百万。

examples.en: She is highly estimated by her colleagues.
examples.cn: 她受到同事们的高度评价。

examples.en: The repair shop gave us a free estimate.
examples.cn: 修理店给我们免费报了个价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「estimate」读起来像「爱是提么特」——不确定时就先估一个数；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aestimare（估价、判断）→ estimate，核心义「给不确定的事物定一个近似价值」。

sensesIntro.en: Estimate first means guess an amount, then judge a person's worth, and as a noun it names a written price.
sensesIntro.cn: estimate 先指估算数量，再指评价人的价值，作名词时指书面报价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number written beside a question mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：问号旁边写下的一个数字。

branches.en: Roughly calculating an amount is the main sense.
branches.cn: 粗略计算数量是主要义项。

branches.en: Judging worth uses the same valuing act.
branches.cn: 评价价值用的是同一种估价行为。

branches.en: The noun is the price on paper.
branches.cn: 名词指纸面上的报价。

branches.en: A written estimate records a calculation.
branches.cn: 书面报价记录了一次估算。

branches.en: Estimating numbers and estimating people both require judgment.
branches.cn: 估算数字与评价人都需要判断。

intro.en: Estimate comes from Latin aestimare, to value, with the noun suffix -ate.
intro.cn: estimate 源自拉丁语 aestimare（估价），带名词性词尾 -ate。

latinIntro.en: Latin aestimare means to value or rate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aestimare 意为估价或评定。

items.example: Aestimare is the Latin source.
Aestimatio gives the noun idea.
Estimate is both verb and noun.
items.exampleCN: estimate 既是动词也是名词。

items.example: The ending -ate shapes the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 塑造动词形式。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms estimation.
Estimation names the judgment.
Over- means too much.
Overestimate means set the number too high.
items.exampleCN: overestimate 意为把数字估得过高。

items.example: Under- means too little.
Underestimate means set the number too low.
items.exampleCN: underestimate 意为把数字估得过低。

definition_zh: 夏眠；夏蛰；花被卷叠式
definition_en: a state of deep summer dormancy in which an animal slows down to survive heat and drought
core_image: 烈日下的泥洞里，一只蜗牛封住壳口，一动不动地等雨
scene: 旱季的池塘干裂，一只青蛙钻进泥里，用黏液封住身体。In the dry season, the frog survives by estivation until the rains return.
sceneCN: 这里 estivation 是「夏眠」（第 1 个义项：动物在炎热干旱季节的休眠状态）；句意：旱季里，这只青蛙靠夏眠撑到雨水回来。

derivatives.zh: 由 estivation 逆构的动词，夏眠；以休眠状态度夏
由拉丁语 aestivus 而来，夏季的

senses.title: Summer dormancy
senses.definition: a sleeplike state in which an animal passes the hot, dry season
senses.definitionCN: 动物度过炎热干旱季节的类睡眠状态
senses.example: The desert snail survives the drought in estivation.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠蜗牛以夏眠状态熬过干旱。
senses.why: The Latin verb aestivare means to spend the summer, so the noun names the state of passing summer in a slowed body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 aestivare 意为「度夏」，因此这个词指以减缓下来的身体状态度过夏天。

senses.title: The act of passing the summer dormant
senses.definition: the behaviour or period of remaining inactive through the hot season
senses.definitionCN: 在炎热季节保持不活动的行为或时段
senses.example: Scientists tracked the frog through its estivation in the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家追踪了这只青蛙在泥中度过的夏眠期。
senses.why: Because the word names an event as well as a state, it can refer to the whole period of summer inactivity, not only to one moment of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指状态也指事件，所以能指整段夏季不活动的时期，而不只是其中一个瞬间。

senses.title: Floral arrangement in the bud
senses.definition: the way petals and sepals are folded in a flower bud
senses.definitionCN: 花瓣与萼片在花芽中的卷叠排列方式
senses.example: Botanists describe the estivation of the sepals in the bud.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家描述萼片在花芽中的卷叠方式。
senses.why: Botany borrowed the same Latin noun aestivatio for the folded arrangement of flower parts; the link to summer is a historical naming convention rather than a clear step of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 植物学沿用同一个拉丁名词 aestivatio，专指花部在花芽中的卷叠排列；它与夏季的联系属于历史命名沿用，并非清晰的语义引申。

intro.en: Estivation comes from Latin aestas, summer, through the verb aestivare, to spend the summer.
intro.cn: estivation 来自拉丁语 aestas（夏天），经动词 aestivare（度夏）而来。

items.en: Aestas means summer and names the hot season itself.
items.cn: aestas 意为夏天，直接指炎热的季节。

items.en: Aestivus is the adjective for things of summer.
items.cn: aestivus 是表示「夏季的」的形容词。

items.en: Aestivare means to spend or pass the summer.
items.cn: aestivare 意为度过夏天。

items.en: Aestivatio names a summering and later a summer sleep.
items.cn: aestivatio 指度夏，后来也指夏季的休眠。

items.en: Botanists use aestivatio for the folding of flower parts in the bud.
items.cn: 植物学家用 aestivatio 指花部在花芽中的卷叠。

items.en: English estivation names summer dormancy, with aestivation as the British spelling.
items.cn: 英语 estivation 指夏眠，英式拼写为 aestivation。

note.en: Estivation belongs to the Latin summer family and pairs naturally with the winter word hibernation.
note.cn: estivation 属于拉丁语「夏天」词族，与表示冬眠的 hibernation 正好成对。

entries.definition: the British spelling of estivation
entries.definitionCN: estivation 的英式拼写，词源完全相同

entries.definition: to pass the summer in a dormant state
relating to summer
entries.definitionCN: 夏季的，与 estivation 同出拉丁语 aestas

entries.definition: winter dormancy in animals
a period of slowed activity
a state of very low activity

normalIntro.en: Estivation is summer turned into sleep: the animal simply waits out the heat.
normalIntro.cn: estivation 是把夏天过成一场睡眠：动物靠等待熬过酷热。

normal.en: Estivation is the summer counterpart of hibernation.
normal.cn: estivation 是 hibernation 的夏季对应词。

normal.en: Snails and frogs may enter estivation when the ground dries.
normal.cn: 地面干透时，蜗牛和青蛙可能进入夏眠。

normal.en: The estivation period lasts until the first heavy rain.
normal.cn: 夏眠期一直持续到第一场大雨。

normal.en: Estivate is the verb built from estivation.
normal.cn: estivate 是由 estivation 构成的动词。

normal.en: The same Latin root gives aestival, a word for summer things.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词根还给出 aestival，指夏季的事物。

abstract.en: Picture a snail sealing its shell with a papery lid and waiting under the cracked earth.
abstract.cn: 想象蜗牛用一层薄盖封住壳口，在龟裂的土地下等待。（对应第 1 个义项：夏眠是一种减缓下来的状态）

abstract.en: Picture a whole hot season passing while the animal barely moves.
abstract.cn: 想象整个炎热的季节过去，而动物几乎不动。（对应第 2 个义项：夏眠也是一整段度夏行为）

abstract.en: Picture petals folded neatly inside a bud, each one tucked in a fixed order.
abstract.cn: 想象花瓣在花芽里整齐地收拢，每一片都按固定的次序叠好。（对应第 3 个义项：花被卷叠式借用了同一个拉丁名词）

examples.en: The frog spent the dry months in estivation.
examples.cn: 这只青蛙在干旱的几个月里一直夏眠。

examples.en: Estivation allows desert animals to survive extreme heat.
examples.cn: 夏眠让沙漠动物得以熬过极端高温。

examples.en: After the rain, the snails came out of estivation.
examples.cn: 雨后，蜗牛结束了夏眠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱睡未醒」——天气太热，干脆一直睡到雨来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aestas（夏天）→ aestivus（夏季的）→ aestivare（度夏）→ aestivatio（度夏；夏眠）→ 英语 estivation，核心义「把夏天睡过去」。

sensesIntro.en: Estivation names first the dormant state, then the whole summer period of inactivity, and finally a botanical term for folded flower parts.
sensesIntro.cn: estivation 先指夏季的休眠状态，再指整段不活动的度夏期，最后是植物学中花部卷叠的术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed shell under cracked earth, waiting for rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：龟裂土地下一只封口的壳，静静等雨。

branches.en: The dormant state is the core sense.
branches.cn: 休眠状态是核心义项。

branches.en: The whole inactive season is the event sense.
branches.cn: 整段不活动的季节是事件义项。

branches.en: The botanical term borrows the same Latin noun.
branches.cn: 植物学术语沿用了同一个拉丁名词。

branches.en: State and period are two views of the same summer sleep.
branches.cn: 状态与时段是同一场夏眠的两种看法。

branches.en: Both senses keep the old summer frame, one seasonal and one botanical.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留「夏季」框架，一个属于季节，一个属于植物学。

intro.en: Estivation is built on Latin aestas, summer, with English estivate and aestival around it.
intro.cn: estivation 建立在拉丁语 aestas（夏天）之上，周围有英语 estivate 与 aestival。

latinIntro.en: Aestas means summer, and aestivare means to spend the summer.
latinIntro.cn: aestas 意为夏天，aestivare 意为度夏。

items.example: Aestas is the season at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: aestas 是这个词的核心季节。

items.example: Aestivus describes summer things.
Aestivare supplies the verb idea.
Aestivatio is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: aestivatio 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: English keeps estivation for the summer dormancy.
items.exampleCN: 英语用 estivation 表示夏眠。

items.example: Estivate is the verb formed from the noun.
items.exampleCN: estivate 是由名词构成的动词。

items.example: Aestival describes summer conditions.
The suffix -ation forms estivation.
Aestivation is the British spelling of the word.
items.exampleCN: aestivation 是这个词的英式拼写。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms estivate.

definition_zh: 使疏远；使不再亲近；使（夫妻）分居
definition_en: to make someone stop feeling close, friendly, or loyal to another person or group
core_image: 两人之间原本相连的线被慢慢拉长，直到断掉
scene: 兄弟俩为了一笔遗产争吵，多年不再来往。A bitter quarrel over the inheritance estranged the two brothers.
sceneCN: 这里 estrange 是「使疏远」（第 1 个义项：使某人不再亲近、友好）；句意：一场关于遗产的激烈争吵使兄弟俩疏远了。

pos.zh: 使疏远；使不再亲近；使分居

derivatives.zh: estrange 加后缀 -ment 构成，疏远；离间；分居
estrange 加后缀 -er 构成，使人疏远的人，属罕用词

senses.title: To alienate a person
senses.definition: to make someone stop feeling close or affectionate toward another person
senses.definitionCN: 使某人不再对另一个人感到亲近或亲密
senses.example: Years of silence had estranged him from his closest friend.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的沉默使他与最亲密的朋友疏远了。
senses.why: The Latin verb extraneare means to make someone foreign, so estranging a friend turns a familiar person into a stranger.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 extraneare 意为「使变成外人」，所以使朋友疏远，就是把熟悉的人变成陌生人。

senses.title: To cut off from a group
senses.definition: to make a person or group feel separate from a community, institution, or cause
senses.definitionCN: 使某人对群体、机构或事业产生隔膜、不再有归属感
senses.example: Rigid rules estranged many young members from the club.
senses.exampleCN: 僵硬的规矩使许多年轻成员对俱乐部产生了离心。
senses.why: The same image works at group scale: a person is pushed outside the circle and becomes an outsider.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象在群体层面同样成立：人被推到圈子之外，成了局外人。

senses.title: To separate married people
senses.definition: to cause a married couple to live apart, used especially in legal contexts
senses.definitionCN: 使夫妻分开生活，尤用于法律语境
senses.example: The court papers describe the couple as estranged for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭文件写明这对夫妻已分居两年。
senses.why: Legal usage applies the making-foreign image to marriage: two people who once shared a home become strangers under one roof.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把「使变成外人」的意象用到婚姻上：曾经同住一屋的两个人，在同一屋檐下成了陌生人。

intro.en: Estrange comes from Latin extraneus, foreign, through extraneare, to make foreign, and Old French estrangier.
intro.cn: estrange 来自拉丁语 extraneus（外来的），经 extraneare（使变成外人）与古法语 estrangier 而来。

items.en: Extra means outside, beyond the boundary.
items.cn: extra 意为在外面、越过边界。

items.en: Extraneus means foreign or belonging to the outside.
items.cn: extraneus 意为外来的、属于外部的。

items.en: Extraneare means to make someone foreign or to alienate.
items.cn: extraneare 意为使某人变成外人、使疏离。

items.en: Estrangier means to remove or to alienate a person.
items.cn: estrangier 意为使人离开、使疏远。

items.en: The English verb appears as estraungen, to alienate.
items.cn: 英语动词以 estraungen 的形式出现，意为使疏远。

items.en: Modern English adds the legal sense of separating spouses.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了使夫妻分居的法律义。

note.en: Estrange shares its root with strange and sits beside the alienate family.
note.cn: estrange 与 strange 同根，并与表示疏离的词相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being alienated
unfamiliar or odd
entries.definitionCN: 陌生的；奇怪的，与 estrange 同出拉丁语 extraneus

entries.definition: not essential, coming from outside
entries.definitionCN: 无关的；外来的，与 estrange 同出拉丁语 extraneus

entries.definition: to make someone feel unwelcome or hostile
to keep someone apart from others
to become or make less friendly
entries.definitionCN: 使关系疏远；与……保持距离

normalIntro.en: Estrange is the verb for turning a familiar face into a stranger.
normalIntro.cn: estrange 是把熟人变成陌生人的那个动词。

normal.en: To estrange a friend is to push that friend away.
normal.cn: estrange a friend 就是把朋友推开。

normal.en: Estranged couples live apart after the marriage breaks down.
normal.cn: 感情破裂后，分居的夫妻各自生活。

normal.en: Estrangement is the noun for the cold space left behind.
normal.cn: estrangement 是这段冷淡距离的名词。

normal.en: Strange and estrange share the idea of being outside.
normal.cn: strange 与 estrange 共享「在外面」的意思。

normal.en: Estrange often appears with from, as in estranged from family.
normal.cn: estrange 常与 from 连用，如 estranged from family。

abstract.en: Picture a thread between two people pulled longer and longer until it snaps.
abstract.cn: 想象两人之间的线被越拉越长，直到绷断。（对应第 1 个义项：疏远就是亲近感被拉断）

abstract.en: Picture a person standing outside a lit circle of friends, looking in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在一圈明亮的朋友之外，只能往里看。（对应第 2 个义项：离心就是被推到圈子外）

abstract.en: Picture two people in one house walking past each other without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象同一屋里的两个人擦肩而过，一言不发。（对应第 3 个义项：分居就是把同屋人变成陌生人）

examples.en: The long dispute estranged the two families.
examples.cn: 长期的纠纷使这两家人疏远了。

examples.en: He felt estranged from his colleagues after the transfer.
examples.cn: 调岗之后，他觉得自己与同事疏远了。

examples.en: The couple had been estranged for a year before the divorce.
examples.cn: 离婚前，这对夫妻已分居一年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一石拦着」——两人中间横着一块石头，来往就断了，于是疏远；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 extra（外面）→ extraneus（外来的）→ extraneare（使变成外人）→ 古法语 estrangier → 中古英语 estraungen → 英语 estrange，核心义「把熟人变成外人」。

sensesIntro.en: Estrange moves from one close relationship to a whole community, and finally to the legal separation of spouses.
sensesIntro.cn: estrange 从一段亲密关系扩展到整个群体，最后落到夫妻分居的法律用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread between two people pulled until it breaks.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人之间的线被拉到断裂。

branches.en: Alienating one person is the first sense.
branches.cn: 疏远一个人是第一个义项。

branches.en: Losing a community is the group-scale sense.
branches.cn: 脱离群体是群体层面的义项。

branches.en: Legal separation of spouses is the formal sense.
branches.cn: 夫妻分居是正式用法中的义项。

branches.en: Both senses push a person outside a circle of belonging.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把人推到归属圈之外。

branches.en: Whether the circle is a club or a marriage, the bond becomes foreign.
branches.cn: 无论圈子里是俱乐部还是婚姻，联结都变得陌生。

intro.en: Estrange is built on Latin extra, outside, and English pairs it with strange, estrangement, and extraneous.
intro.cn: estrange 建立在拉丁语 extra（外面）之上，英语里与 strange、estrangement、extraneous 相邻。

latinIntro.en: Extra means outside, extraneus means foreign, and extraneare means to make foreign.
latinIntro.cn: extra 意为在外面，extraneus 意为外来的，extraneare 意为使变成外人。

items.example: Extra puts the image outside the boundary.
items.exampleCN: extra 把意象放到边界之外。

items.example: Extraneus gives the sense of being an outsider.
items.exampleCN: extraneus 给出局外人的意思。

items.example: Extraneare is the verb behind estrange.
items.exampleCN: extraneare 是 estrange 背后的动词。

items.example: Old French estrangier carries the verb onward.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 estrangier 把动词继续带下去。

items.example: English estrange keeps the verb sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语 estrange 保留动词含义。

items.example: The noun estrangement names the result.
The suffix -ment forms estrangement.
Strange is a cousin from the same root.
Extraneous keeps the outside idea.
Estranger is a rare agent noun.
items.exampleCN: estranger 是罕见的施动名词。

definition_zh: 河口湾（河流入海口淡水与海水混合的宽阔水域）；潮汐河口；河口生态系统
definition_en: the wide lower part of a river where fresh water meets the sea and is mixed by the tides
core_image: 浑黄的河水在喇叭形的入海口被咸蓝的海水顶回来，潮水一涨一落，泥滩时而淹没时而露出
scene: 退潮后，喇叭形的入海口露出大片泥滩，海鸥沿着浅水道觅食。At low tide the estuary exposed wide mudflats where gulls fed along shallow channels.
sceneCN: 这里 estuary 指「河流入海处淡水与海水交汇的宽阔水域」（第 1 个义项：河口湾）；句意：退潮时，这片河口湾露出大片泥滩，海鸥在浅水道旁觅食。图中可辨识物件：泥滩上的浅水道、觅食的海鸥、河与海交界处的水色、搁浅的小船。

pos.zh: 河口湾；河口（河流入海处淡水与海水交汇、受潮汐影响的水域）

forms.label: 形容词（河口湾的，较少用）

derivatives.zh: 河口湾的；生活在河口湾的
河口湾的（较少用的同义变体）
河口英语（泰晤士河口一带的英语口音）
河口湾口门（河流与海相接的出口）
河口环境（淡咸水交汇的生境）

senses.title: The wide mouth where river meets sea
senses.titleCN: 河口湾：河流入海处的宽阔水域
senses.definition: the wide lower reach of a river where its fresh water meets and mixes with sea water
senses.definitionCN: 河流下游宽阔的河段，淡水在此与海水相遇并混合
senses.example: At low tide the estuary exposed wide mudflats where gulls fed along shallow channels.
senses.exampleCN: 退潮时，这片河口湾露出大片泥滩，海鸥在浅水道旁觅食。
senses.why: the word names the drowned lower valley itself, a body of water wider than the river because the sea has invaded it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指被海水侵入的下游河谷本身；因为海水的进入，它比河道更宽。

senses.title: A tidal reach governed by the tide
senses.definition: the part of a river near its mouth in which the water level and the direction of flow reverse with the tide
senses.definitionCN: 河流近口门、水位与流向随潮汐往复变化的那一段
senses.example: Salt water pushes upstream in the estuary with every flood tide.
senses.exampleCN: 每次涨潮，咸水都沿河口段向上游推进。
senses.why: the tidal sense narrows the first: the same water body is defined by the twice-daily reversal of its current.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐义收窄了第一个义项：同一片水域，以水流一日两次反向为界定特征。

senses.title: A brackish ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 河口生态系统（淡咸水交汇的生境）
senses.definition: the community of plants and animals adapted to water whose salinity changes with the tide
senses.definitionCN: 适应盐度随潮汐变化的河口水的动植物群落
senses.example: Juvenile salmon feed in the estuary before they enter the open sea.
senses.exampleCN: 幼鲑在进入外海之前先在河口育肥。
senses.why: from the place the word passes to what lives in it, a standard shift from a habitat to its community.
senses.whyCN: 由地点转向其中的生物，这是从生境到生物群落的常见转喻。

senses.title: Silt laid down at the river mouth
senses.titleCN: 河口沉积（河流泥沙在口门堆积）
senses.definition: sand and mud carried down by the river and deposited where the current slows at the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 河流带下的砂与泥在口门流速减缓处堆积而成的沉积物
senses.example: Cores from the estuary record two centuries of upstream soil erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 河口沉积柱芯记录了两个世纪的上游水土流失。
senses.why: the estuary is a sediment trap, so its name transfers to the material that fills it.
senses.whyCN: 河口是泥沙的捕集器，因此其名称也转指填在其中的物质。

senses.title: Fishing and farming in estuarine water
senses.definition: the use of nutrient-rich estuarine water for catching fish or cultivating shellfish
senses.definitionCN: 利用营养丰富的河口水域捕鱼或养殖贝类
senses.example: Oyster farms in the estuary depend on clean water and steady tides.
senses.exampleCN: 河口湾的牡蛎养殖场依赖洁净的水与稳定的潮汐。
senses.why: human activity is named by its setting, as with any fishery; the estuary supplies the nutrients that make the catch possible.
senses.whyCN: 人类活动以所在地命名，正如各类渔场；河口提供养分，才使捕捞成为可能。

senses.title: Pollution where the river meets the sea
senses.definition: the accumulation of pollutants in estuarine water, where river discharge and sea water mix and currents are slow
senses.definitionCN: 污染物在河口水中的累积，该处河水与海水混合、流速缓慢
senses.example: Nitrogen from farms collects in the estuary and feeds summer algal blooms.
senses.exampleCN: 农田带来的氮在河口积聚，助长夏季藻华。
senses.why: because the estuary is the collecting basin of a whole catchment, its name becomes shorthand for the water-quality problem there.
senses.whyCN: 河口是整个流域的汇集盆，因此其名称成为当地水质问题的代称。

senses.title: A dredged channel for shipping
senses.definition: the navigable channel maintained through an estuary for ships moving between the river and the sea
senses.definitionCN: 为船舶进出河流与海洋而在河口维护的通航水道
senses.example: Dredging keeps the estuary open to ships drawing twelve metres.
senses.exampleCN: 疏浚使河口航道可供吃水十二米的船舶通行。
senses.why: the mouth is the gate of a river port, so the word also names the passage that has to be kept open.
senses.whyCN: 口门是河港的门户，因此这个词也指必须维持畅通的那条通道。

senses.title: A meeting ground of unlike things
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：不同事物的交汇地带
senses.definition: a place or situation in which two different systems meet and influence each other
senses.definitionCN: 两种不同体系相遇并相互影响的地方或处境
senses.example: The festival became an estuary of rural and urban tastes.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆成了乡村与城市趣味的交汇地带。
senses.why: the physical mixing of fresh and salt water is generalized into any boundary zone where unlike things blend.
senses.whyCN: 淡水与咸水的物理混合被一般化为任何不同事物交融的边界地带。

intro.en: Estuary comes from Latin aestuarium 'a tract flooded by the tide', from aestus 'tide, surge, heat'. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century. The deeper origin of aestus is uncertain, and the link sometimes proposed with aestas 'summer' is a hypothesis.
intro.cn: estuary 来自拉丁 aestuarium「受潮水淹没的滩地」，后者出自 aestus「潮汐、涌动、热」。英语于 16 世纪借入。aestus 的更深来源不确定，有人提出它与 aestas「夏天」有关，但那只是假说。

items.en: Aestus meant 'tide, surge' and also 'boiling, seething heat'. Roman writers used it for both the movement of the sea and the fever of the body.
items.cn: aestus 意为「潮汐、涌动」，也指「沸腾、灼热」。罗马作家用它既指海水的运动，也指身体的发热。

items.en: Aestuarium was the low ground or channel that the tide fills and empties; the suffix -arium marks a place associated with the action of aestus.
items.cn: aestuarium 指潮水灌入又退出的低地或水道；后缀 -arium 表示与 aestus 这一动作相关的地点。

items.en: English geographers borrowed aestuarium in the 1530s for the widened mouth of a tidal river, and the spelling settled as estuary.
items.cn: 16 世纪 30 年代，英国地理学者借入 aestuarium，用来指受潮汐影响的宽河口；拼写后来固定为 estuary。

items.en: The early English sense kept the tidal idea, so an estuary was a river mouth shaped by the rise and fall of the sea rather than merely the end of a river.
items.cn: 早期英语义保留了潮汐意味，因此河口湾指受海水涨落塑造的河口，而不只是河流的终点。

items.en: The adjective estuarine was formed in the nineteenth century on the model of Latin -inus, and estuarial followed as a rarer variant; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 estuarine 于 19 世纪仿拉丁 -inus 构成，estuarial 作为更少用的变体随后出现；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of aestus): the connection with aestas 'summer' and with Greek aithein 'to burn' are competing hypotheses, and any Indo-European form offered for aestus is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（aestus 的更深词源）：与 aestas「夏天」以及希腊 aithein「燃烧」的联系是并行的假说，凡为 aestus 拟出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates estuary from look-alikes, including one word that shares its Latin root and several that do not; group two contrasts the tidal river mouth with neighbouring water features.
note.cn: 第一组把 estuary 与形近词分开，其中一词共享拉丁词根，其余并无关系；第二组把潮汐河口与相邻的水域概念作对比。

entries.definition: From Latin aestivus 'of summer', built on the same aest- base as aestus; it means 'summery' and does not name a river mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 aestivus「夏天的」，与 aestus 共用 aest- 词干；意为「夏季的」，并不指河口。

entries.definition: The practice of lending money at interest, from Latin usura 'use'; the -ury ending makes it sound like estuary, but the roots differ.
entries.definitionCN: 指放贷取息的行业，来自拉丁 usura「使用」；-ury 词尾使它听起来像 estuary，但词根不同。

entries.definition: To alienate someone, from Latin extraneare 'treat as a stranger'; only the opening letters resemble estuary.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某人疏远，来自拉丁 extraneare「当作陌生人对待」；只有开头几个字母与 estuary 相似。

entries.definition: Concerned with beauty, from Greek aisthanesthai 'to perceive'; the shared opening sound is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指与美有关的，来自希腊 aisthanesthai「感知」；开头的读音相近只是巧合。

entries.definition: A river mouth where the current slows and splits around deposited sediment; an estuary is instead a drowned valley dominated by tides.
entries.definitionCN: 河流因流速减缓、泥沙堆积而分汊的口门；河口湾则是被海水淹没、以潮汐为主导的河谷。

entries.definition: A Scottish word for a narrow sea inlet or river estuary; it overlaps with estuary but is regional.
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰语中指狭窄的海湾或河口；与 estuary 语义重叠，但属地域用词。

entries.definition: A narrow opening by which the sea enters the land; it need not receive a river, which an estuary always does.
entries.definitionCN: 海水伸入陆地的狭窄通道；它不一定有河流注入，而河口湾一定有。

entries.definition: The point where a river enters a larger body of water; it is neutral and does not imply tidal mixing or width.
entries.definitionCN: 河流进入更大水域的那一点；语气中立，不含潮汐混合或宽阔水域之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aestus 'tide' plus -arium 'place': the place that the tide fills and empties.
normal.cn: aestus「潮汐」加 -arium「地点」：潮水灌入又退出的那个地方。

normal.en: The family is estuary, estuarine and estuarial; the adjective is far more common in ecology than the noun is in speech.
normal.cn: 同族词是 estuary、estuarine 与 estuarial；形容词在生态学中的使用远多于名词在日常口语中的使用。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the ecology: estuary ecosystem, estuary sediment, estuary pollution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出生态义：河口生态系统、河口沉积物、河口污染。

normal.en: Geography pairs it with delta: a delta builds outward, while an estuary is a valley drowned inward by the sea.
normal.cn: 地理学把它与三角洲对举：三角洲向外堆出，河口湾则是被海水向内淹没的河谷。

normal.en: British references such as the Thames estuary and the Severn estuary name the tidal type most clearly.
normal.cn: 泰晤士河口与塞文河口这类英国实例最能说明潮汐河口这一类型。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway where two crowds push in opposite directions and neither can move freely.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门口，两股人潮相向而行，谁也走不痛快。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of tea into which cold milk is poured: the boundary is where the colours first mix.
abstract.cn: 想象往一杯热茶里倒入冷牛奶：交界处正是两种颜色最先混开的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a market where two languages trade words across the same counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个市场，两种语言在同一个柜台前交换词语。

examples.en: The estuary supports a nursery for young fish before they reach the open sea.
examples.cn: 这片河口湾为幼鱼提供育肥场所，之后它们才进入外海。

examples.en: Sediment cores from the estuary show how fast the surrounding hills eroded.
examples.cn: 取自河口的沉积柱芯显示周边山地侵蚀得有多快。

examples.en: Ships wait for high water before they enter the shallow estuary.
examples.cn: 船舶等高潮时才驶入这片浅水河口湾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「estuary」读似「爱水求瑞」——河水一路爱水，到海口求个汇合之处，便是河口湾

root: 拉丁 aestuarium「高潮淹没的滩地」< aestus「潮汐、沸腾、热」；英语 16 世纪借入。aestus 更深来源不确定，与 aestas「夏天」及希腊 aithein「燃烧」的联系均属假说，非定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one physical event: a river valley drowned by the sea, where fresh and salt water are stirred twice a day. From that place come the tidal reach, the brackish community, its sediment, its fisheries, its pollution, its shipping channel, and finally any zone where two worlds mix.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一个自然事件展开：河谷被海水淹没，淡水与咸水一日两次被搅动。由此依次生出潮汐河段、淡咸水生物群落、河口沉积、渔业、污染、航道，最后泛指任何两个世界交融的地带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river mouth flooded by the tide, where fresh and salt water are stirred together.
core.cn: 核心意象：被潮水灌入的河口，淡水与咸水在此搅在一起。

branches.en: DROWNED MOUTH: the widened lower valley and its twice-daily reversal of flow.
branches.cn: 被淹的口门：加宽的下游河谷，以及一日两次反向的水流。

branches.en: BRACKISH COMMUNITY: the living community that tolerates shifting salinity.
branches.cn: 淡咸水群落：能耐受盐度变化的生物群落。

branches.en: SILT TRAP: the mouth as a basin where river sediment settles.
branches.cn: 泥沙捕集：口门作为河流沉积物沉降的盆地。

branches.en: WORKING WATER: fishing, pollution and navigation all concentrate at the same mouth.
branches.cn: 作业水域：渔业、污染与航运都集中在这同一个口门。

branches.en: MEETING GROUND: the physical mix becomes an image for any boundary between two systems.
branches.cn: 交汇地带：物理混合成为任何两个体系边界的意象。

intro.en: Estuary is a Latin loan whose parts can still be read: the root aestus 'tide' plus the place suffix -arium. English then added -ine and -al for the adjectives and joined the noun to native nouns in compounds.
intro.cn: estuary 是拉丁借词，其构词成分仍可读出：词根 aestus「潮汐」加地点后缀 -arium。英语随后加 -ine 与 -al 构成形容词，并与本族名词组合成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aestus gives aestuarium and the verb aestuare 'to surge, boil'. Latin aestas 'summer' is a possible relative, but the link is debated rather than established.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aestus 衍生 aestuarium 与动词 aestuare「涌动、沸腾」。拉丁 aestas「夏天」可能是其亲属，但这一联系仍有争议，尚未确立。

items.example: Aestus is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: aestus 是整个词族的词根。

items.meaning: a place associated with an action
items.example: The suffix turns an action into a place.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一个动作变成一处地点。

items.example: The estuary opens into a cold sea.
items.exampleCN: 这片河口湾通向一片寒冷的海。

items.example: Estuarine mud supports dense worm populations.
items.exampleCN: 河口湾的淤泥养育了密集的沙蚕种群。

items.meaning: of an estuary, a rarer variant
items.example: Estuarial waters warm slowly in spring.
items.exampleCN: 河口湾水域在春季升温缓慢。

items.meaning: the outer opening of a tidal river
items.example: Fishing boats crossed the estuary mouth at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 渔船在黎明时越过河口湾口门。

items.meaning: a brackish habitat within an estuary
items.meaningCN: 河口湾内的淡咸水生境
items.example: The estuarine habitat shifts with every tide.
items.exampleCN: 河口的生境随每次潮汐而改变。

items.meaning: an estuary dominated by tidal flow
items.meaningCN: 以潮汐水流为主导的河口
items.example: A tidal estuary reverses its current twice a day.
items.exampleCN: 潮汐河口的水流一日两次反向。

items.meaning: a variety of English associated with the Thames estuary
items.meaningCN: 与泰晤士河口相关的英语口音
items.example: Estuary English spread far beyond its home region.
items.exampleCN: 河口英语传播到了其发源地区之外很远的地方。

definition_zh: 永恒的；永存的；无休止的；始终不变的
definition_en: lasting for ever, with no beginning or end, or seeming never to stop
core_image: 一条既没有起点也没有终点的线，一直伸到看不见的地方
scene: 老人指着墙上的灯说，它从他出生之前就一直亮着。The old man pointed to the lamp on the wall and said it had burned with an eternal flame since before he was born.
sceneCN: 这里 eternal 是「永恒不灭的」（第 2 个义项：从此刻起永远持续）；句意：老人指着墙上那盏灯说，它从他出生之前起就一直燃着不灭的火焰。

pos.zh: 永恒的；永存的；无休止的；始终不变的

derivatives.zh: 由 eternal 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「永恒；无尽的时间；来世」
由 eternal 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「永恒地；老是」
由 eternal 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使永恒；使不朽」

senses.title: Lasting without beginning or end
senses.definition: existing for ever, with neither a beginning nor an end
senses.definitionCN: 永远存在，既没有开始也没有终结
senses.example: Many religions describe God as eternal.
senses.exampleCN: 许多宗教把神描述为无始无终的存在。
senses.why: Latin aeternus first meant lasting an unmeasured age, so the oldest sense covers time that has no edge in either direction, before or after.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aeternus 最初表示「持续一个无法丈量的年代」，所以最古老的义项覆盖的是前后两端都没有边界的时间。

senses.title: Going on for ever from now
senses.definition: continuing for ever into the future, so that it will never end
senses.definitionCN: 从今往后永远持续，不会结束
senses.example: They promised each other eternal love.
senses.exampleCN: 他们向彼此许诺永恒的爱。
senses.why: Once the part of aeternus that means no end is brought forward, the word can name anything that will never stop from this moment on.
senses.whyCN: 当 aeternus 中「没有终点」的一面被推到前面，这个词就能指任何从此不再停止的事物。

senses.title: Endless and wearisome
senses.definition: seeming to continue without ever stopping, especially in a tedious way
senses.definitionCN: 似乎永远不会停止，尤指令人厌烦地持续
senses.example: His eternal complaints drove the whole office mad.
senses.exampleCN: 他没完没了的抱怨把整个办公室都逼疯了。
senses.why: An endless thing never reaches a stopping point, so speakers borrow the word for annoyances that feel as if they will never end.
senses.whyCN: 无止境的事物永远到不了停下的一刻，于是人们借用这个词来形容那些让人觉得永远不会结束的烦心事。

senses.title: Unchanging across all ages
senses.titleCN: 始终不变的；万古不易的
senses.definition: true or valid in every age, not changed by the passing of time
senses.definitionCN: 在任何时代都成立，不随流逝的时间改变
senses.example: Mathematicians treat some results as eternal truths.
senses.exampleCN: 数学家把某些结论视为永恒真理。
senses.why: What has no boundary in time has no point at which it could change, so eternal also means valid in every age.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上没有边界的东西，也没有任何一个点可以改变，因此 eternal 又表示「在任何时代都成立」。

intro.en: Eternal goes back to Latin aevum, an age or a lifetime, and to aeternus, lasting an unmeasured age.
intro.cn: eternal 可追到拉丁语 aevum（年代、一生）与 aeternus（持续一个无法丈量的年代）。

items.en: A root carrying the sense of life force or long life lies behind the words for age.
items.cn: 一个带有「生命力、长寿」意味的古老词根，是「年代」一词的来源。

items.en: Aevum means an age or a lifetime, a stretch of time.
items.cn: aevum 意为年代或一生，即一段长度可长可短的时间。

items.en: Aeternus, probably built on aevum, means lasting an age that cannot be measured.
items.cn: aeternus 一般认为由 aevum 构成，意为「持续一个无法丈量的年代」。

items.en: Aeternitas names endless duration as an abstract quality.
items.cn: aeternitas 把「无尽的时间」抽象成一种性质。

items.en: Eternel carries the adjective from Latin into French.
items.cn: 古法语 eternel 把这个形容词从拉丁语带入法语。

items.en: English eternal keeps the sense of time without edges and adds the casual sense of an endless annoyance.
items.cn: 英语 eternal 保留「时间没有边界」的意思，又增加了「烦得没完没了」的口语义。

note.en: Eternal sits in a family of time words, with eternity beside it and Latin sempiternal as a close cousin.
note.cn: eternal 位于一组时间词之中，旁边有 eternity，拉丁来源的 sempiternal 则是近亲。

entries.definition: time without end, or the state of lasting for ever
entries.definitionCN: 无尽的时间；永恒的状态

entries.definition: for ever, or all the time
lasting for ever, with Latin semper, always, added to the same root
entries.definitionCN: 永久的；由拉丁语 semper（始终）加同一词根构成

entries.definition: lasting for ever and never coming to an end
never ending, or happening again and again
not changed or affected by the passing of time
entries.definitionCN: 超越时间的；不受时间影响的

normalIntro.en: Eternal carries Latin aevum, an age, so every sense turns on time that ordinary years cannot measure.
normalIntro.cn: eternal 带着拉丁语 aevum（年代）的影子，所以每个义项都围绕「普通年数无法丈量的时间」展开。

normal.en: Eternal and eternity share one root, so both name time without edges.
normal.cn: eternal 与 eternity 同根，两者都指没有边界的时间。

normal.en: Eternal life and eternal love are the collocations that learners meet first.
normal.cn: eternal life 与 eternal love 是学习者最先遇到的搭配。

normal.en: Sempiternal adds Latin semper, always, to the same old root.
normal.cn: sempiternal 在同一个古老词根上加了拉丁语 semper（始终）。

normal.en: The adverb eternally often carries the complaint sense, as in eternally late.
normal.cn: 副词 eternally 常带抱怨色彩，例如老是迟到。

normal.en: Compare everlasting: eternal stresses having no boundary at all, everlasting stresses going on without end.
normal.cn: 对比 everlasting：eternal 强调根本没有边界，everlasting 强调一直持续下去。

abstract.en: Picture a ring with no seam: it never begins and never ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚没有接缝的环：既没有开始，也没有结束。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock whose hands move but never reach a final hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，指针一直走，却永远到不了最后一个小时。

abstract.en: Think of a dripping tap at night that will not stop.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一只滴水的龙头，怎么也停不下来。

examples.en: The poem speaks of eternal life after death.
examples.cn: 这首诗谈到死后的永生。

examples.en: Their eternal love story has been told for a hundred years.
examples.cn: 他们那段永恒的爱情故事已被传诵一百年。

examples.en: He was tired of his neighbour and her eternal questions about money.
examples.cn: 他受够了邻居和她那些没完没了的钱的问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一特浓」——一杯特浓的茶，香气久久不散，像是永远留在嘴里；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aevum（年代、一生）→ aeternus（持续一个无法丈量的年代的）→ aeternitas（永恒）→ 古法语 eternel → 英语 eternal，核心义是「时间没有边界」。

sensesIntro.en: Eternal starts from time with no edge at all, narrows to time that never ends from now on, then spreads to endless annoyance and to truths that no age can change.
sensesIntro.cn: eternal 从「完全没有边界的时间」出发，收窄为「从今往后永不结束」，再扩展到「没完没了的烦扰」和「任何时代都改变不了的真理」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line with no starting point and no finishing point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条既没有起点也没有终点的线。

branches.en: Time with no edge in either direction is the oldest and most religious sense.
branches.cn: 前后都没有边界的时间，是最古老也最带宗教色彩的义项。

branches.en: Never stopping from this moment is the everyday sense of promises and fame.
branches.cn: 从此刻起永不停止，是承诺与名声的日常义项。

branches.en: An annoyance that feels endless borrows the same word.
branches.cn: 让人感到没完没了的烦扰，借用了同一个词。

branches.en: A truth outside passing time is the abstract sense.
branches.cn: 超越流逝时间的真理，是抽象义项。

branches.en: Both the uncreated and the unchanging share the idea of standing outside passing time.
branches.cn: 「无始」与「不变」共享同一个想法：站在流逝的时间之外。

intro.en: Eternal is a Latin time word wearing an English adjective ending, with a small family built on the same root.
intro.cn: eternal 是一个拉丁语时间词加上英语形容词词尾，同一词根上还长出一小族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aevum means an age, and aeternus means lasting an age that cannot be measured.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aevum 意为年代，aeternus 意为持续一个无法丈量的年代。

items.example: Aevum is the time word behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: aevum 是整个词族背后的时间词。

items.meaningCN: 持续无法丈量的年代的
items.example: Aeternus is the direct source of eternal.
items.exampleCN: aeternus 是 eternal 的直接来源。

items.example: Aeternitas names the abstract quality.
Aeternalis passes into Old French.
The ending -al helps shape eternal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 参与构成 eternal。

items.example: Eternal keeps the core sense of no boundary.
items.exampleCN: eternal 保留「没有边界」的核心义。

items.example: Eternity turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: eternity 把这个形容词变成名词。

items.meaningCN: 把形容词变成名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity builds eternity.
Eternally adds the adverb ending -ly.
Eternalize adds the verb ending -ize.

definition_zh: 空灵的；缥缈的；天界的；以太的
definition_en: light, airy, and delicate, as if belonging to the upper air rather than to the earth
core_image: 薄而明亮的空气里飘着一个雾气般的身影，轻得风一吹就散
scene: 舞台上烟雾升起，穿白衣的舞者在灯下几乎透明。On the stage the smoke rose and the dancer in white looked almost ethereal in the light.
sceneCN: 这里 ethereal 是「空灵飘逸的」（第 2 个义项：轻盈细腻、近乎不真实）；句意：舞台上烟雾升起，穿白衣的舞者在灯光下显得近乎空灵。

pos.zh: 空灵的；缥缈的；天界的；以太的

derivatives.zh: 由 ethereal 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「空灵地；轻盈地」
由 ethereal 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「空灵；缥缈」
由 ethereal 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使空灵；使缥缈」

senses.title: Belonging to the upper air
senses.definition: belonging to the bright region above the clouds, or to the heavens
senses.definitionCN: 属于云层之上那片明亮区域或天界的
senses.example: The old poets placed the gods in an ethereal realm above the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 古代诗人把众神安置在云层之上的天界。
senses.why: Greek aither named the bright upper air that people believed filled the sky, so the adjective first described whatever belongs to that region.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aither 指人们相信充满天空的明亮上层空气，因此这个形容词最初描述属于那一区域的事物。

senses.title: Light and delicate, almost unreal
senses.definition: so light, fine, and delicate that it seems not quite of this world
senses.definitionCN: 轻盈、细腻到仿佛不属于这个世界
senses.example: Her ethereal beauty silenced the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 她空灵的美让整个房间安静下来。
senses.why: Because the upper air was thought to be purer than the air we breathe, the word came to praise things that look refined and almost weightless.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们认为上层空气比我们呼吸的空气更纯净，这个词便用来赞美那些看起来精致、几乎失重的事物。

senses.title: Faint and unearthly
senses.definition: thin, faint, and strange, like a shape seen through mist
senses.definitionCN: 稀薄、微弱而奇异，像透过雾气看到的形体
senses.example: An ethereal glow moved slowly across the marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 一团幽微的光缓缓移过沼泽。
senses.why: What belongs to the air is also hard to grasp, so the word slides from delicate to ghostly and barely visible.
senses.whyCN: 属于空气的东西同样难以抓住，于是这个词从「精致」滑向「幽灵般、几乎看不见」。

senses.title: Of ether or the ether
senses.definition: relating to ether, either the supposed medium of space in old physics or the chemical liquid
senses.definitionCN: 与以太有关的，或指旧物理学假想的空间介质，或指化学上的醚
senses.example: Chemists of the time spoke of an ethereal liquid with a sweet smell.
senses.exampleCN: 当时的化学家谈到一种带甜味的醚状液体。
senses.why: When aether became the name of a chemical and of a supposed medium filling space, the adjective followed it into physics and chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 当 aether 成为一种化学物质和一种假想空间介质的名称，这个形容词也跟着进入了物理与化学领域。

intro.en: Ethereal comes from Greek aither, the bright upper air, through Latin aether and aethereus.
intro.cn: ethereal 来自希腊语 aither（明亮的上层空气），经由拉丁语 aether 与 aethereus 进入英语。

items.en: A root carrying the sense of burning or shining is behind the Greek word for the bright sky.
items.cn: 一个带有「燃烧、发光」意味的古老词根，是希腊语中「明亮天空」一词的来源。

items.en: Aither names the pure, bright air above the clouds.
items.cn: aither 指云层之上纯净而明亮的空气。

items.en: Aitherios, the adjective built on it, means of the upper air.
items.cn: 由它构成的形容词 aitherios 意为「属于上层空气的」。

items.en: Aether and aethereus carry the sky word into Latin.
items.cn: aether 与 aethereus 把这个天空之词带入拉丁语。

items.en: English ethereal appears in the seventeenth century for things of the sky, then for delicate beauty.
items.cn: 英语 ethereal 在十七世纪出现，先指天空之物，后指精致轻盈之美。

items.en: Chemistry adds the ether sense when aether names a volatile liquid.
items.cn: 当 aether 又成为一种挥发性液体的名称，化学义也随之加入。

note.en: Ethereal is the adjective of the old sky word aether, with a small family around it and airy words nearby.
note.cn: ethereal 是古老天空词 aether 的形容词形式，它周围有一小族词，旁边还有一批「轻盈」义的近义词。

entries.definition: the upper air, or the chemical liquid once used as an anaesthetic
entries.definitionCN: 以太；上层空气；曾用作麻醉剂的乙醚

entries.definition: in a light, delicate, otherworldly way
to make something light and ethereal in quality
light and open, as if full of moving air
belonging to heaven or to the sky
strange and apparently not of this world

normalIntro.en: Ethereal is built on the Greek word for the bright upper air, so the whole family stays light and sky-like.
normalIntro.cn: ethereal 建立在希腊语「明亮的上层空气」一词上，所以整族词都带着轻盈与天空的气质。

normal.en: The noun ether is the older word: ethereal means of the ether.
normal.cn: 名词 ether 是更早的词：ethereal 就是「属于以太的」。

normal.en: Ethereal beauty and ethereal music are the collocations that carry the delicate sense.
normal.cn: ethereal beauty 与 ethereal music 承载着「精致轻盈」这一层意思。

normal.en: Aether is the Latin spelling that still appears in old science books.
normal.cn: aether 是仍出现在旧科学书里的拉丁语拼法。

normal.en: The adverb ethereally usually describes a voice or a light.
normal.cn: 副词 ethereally 通常用来形容嗓音或光线。

normal.en: Compare airy: airy is everyday and can mean breezy, while ethereal is literary and suggests another world.
normal.cn: 对比 airy：airy 更日常，可指通风的，而 ethereal 偏文学，暗示另一个世界。

abstract.en: Picture a layer of cloud lit from above, far higher than any aeroplane flies.
abstract.cn: 想象一层被上方照亮的云，高过任何飞机能飞到的地方。

abstract.en: Imagine silk so thin that light passes straight through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块薄得让光直接穿过的丝绸。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp seen through fog, bright but with no clear edge.
abstract.cn: 想象透过雾看到的一盏灯，明亮却没有清晰的边缘。

examples.en: The singer has an ethereal voice that seems to come from far away.
examples.cn: 这位歌手的嗓音空灵，仿佛来自很远的地方。

examples.en: Mist gave the garden an ethereal look at dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明时分的薄雾让花园显得缥缈。

examples.en: Victorian scientists argued about the ethereal medium that was said to fill space.
examples.cn: 维多利亚时代的科学家为那种据说充满空间的以太介质争论不休。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一贴柔」——一层柔软的薄纱贴在皮肤上，轻得几乎没有重量；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 aither（明亮的上层空气）→ aitherios（属于上层的）→ 拉丁语 aether / aethereus → 英语 ethereal；词根可追到表示「燃烧、发光」的印欧词根。

sensesIntro.en: Ethereal moves from the bright upper air of Greek cosmology to delicate beauty, then to faint ghostly shapes, and finally to the technical ether of physics and chemistry.
sensesIntro.cn: ethereal 从希腊宇宙观里明亮的上层空气，走到精致轻盈之美，再走到幽微如影的形体，最后进入物理与化学里的「以太」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure of mist drifting in thin, bright air.
core.cn: 核心意象：薄而明亮的空气里飘着一个雾气般的身影。

branches.en: The bright region above the clouds is the oldest cosmic sense.
branches.cn: 云层之上那片明亮区域，是最古老的宇宙论义项。

branches.en: Delicate beauty grew out of the purity of that upper air.
branches.cn: 精致轻盈之美，是从上层空气的纯净感里长出来的。

branches.en: Faint ghostly shapes are the same airiness felt as strangeness.
branches.cn: 幽微如影的形体，是同一种轻盈感被感受为奇异。

branches.en: The technical ether keeps the old noun alive in science.
branches.cn: 技术上的「以太」让这个古老名词在科学里延续下来。

branches.en: Both delicate beauty and ghostly faintness share the idea of almost no weight.
branches.cn: 精致之美与幽微之影共享同一个想法：几乎没有重量。

intro.en: Ethereal is a Greek sky word with a Latin adjective ending, and the noun ether stands beside it.
intro.cn: ethereal 是一个希腊语天空词加上拉丁来源的形容词词尾，名词 ether 就站在它旁边。

latinIntro.en: Greek aither became Latin aether, and the Latin adjective aethereus gave English the ending of ethereal.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 aither 变为拉丁语 aether，拉丁形容词 aethereus 为英语 ethereal 提供了词尾。

items.example: Aither names the pure air above the clouds.
items.exampleCN: aither 指云层之上的纯净空气。

items.example: Aithein supplies the shining idea behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: aithein 为这个名词提供「发光」的意象。

items.example: Aether carries the Greek word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: aether 把这个希腊词带入拉丁语。

items.example: Aethereus is the Latin adjective behind ethereal.
items.exampleCN: aethereus 是 ethereal 背后的拉丁形容词。

items.meaningCN: 源自拉丁语的形容词词尾
items.example: The ending -eal shapes ethereal.
Ethereal keeps both the sky sense and the delicate sense.
items.exampleCN: ethereal 同时保留天空与轻盈两层意思。

items.meaning: the upper air, or a chemical liquid
items.example: Ether is the noun that stands beside the adjective.
items.exampleCN: ether 是与这个形容词并立的名词。

items.example: Ethereally adds the adverb ending -ly.
Etherealize adds the verb ending -ize.
The suffix -al appears in many sky adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 出现在许多与天空有关的形容词里。
